feed.summary: This article analyzes the impact of stock splits on market structure, liquidity, retail investor participation, notional exposure, trade size, odd lots, and volatility in both equities and options markets. Using data from 61 stock splits since 2020, including a case study on Apple (AAPL), the Cboe team found that stock splits do not necessarily increase liquidity proportionally to the split ratio and can lead to a decrease in overall investor capital exposure, though they do increase retail investor participation. The study suggests while splits enhance accessibility, they may not always benefit existing shareholders.

feed.title: Amazon Announces SoCal Expansion, Including 700 Jobs in San Diego
feed.summary: Amazon.com Inc. is expanding its operations in Southern California, creating 2,500 new corporate and technical jobs, with over 700 of those located in San Diego. To accommodate this growth, Amazon has signed a lease for a 123,000-square-foot office space in University Town Center, expected to open in early 2023. The new roles include positions in cloud infrastructure, Alexa development, video game design, software engineering, human resources, finance, and IT.

feed.title: Focus: Amazon's union: Two warehouses, two outcomes
feed.summary: Amazon's two warehouses on Staten Island, JFK8 and LDJ5, despite being near each other and hiring from the same communities, had opposing outcomes on unionization. JFK8 voted to unionize due to worker dissatisfaction with conditions and the efforts of ALU founders who had worked there. LDJ5, a newer facility with different job roles and schedules, rejected unionization, with some workers finding the work easier and expressing concerns about union dues and goals.

feed.title: Amazon says it has too much warehouse space. What's that mean for the broader industrial market?
feed.summary: Amazon.com Inc., a dominant force in the U.S. industrial market, appears to have reached its maximum capacity for warehouse and fulfillment space. This development could signal significant shifts for the broader industrial real estate sector. The article prompts a discussion about the implications of Amazon's changing needs on the overall market.

feed.title: Bridge Point Melrose Park signs big leases for new industrial development
feed.summary: Bridge Industrial has secured its first two tenants, CEVA and Expeditors, for its new industrial development, Bridge Point Melrose Park. The developer adapted during construction to meet the warehouse needs of these major logistics companies. The 87-acre development is strategically located about six miles south of O'Hare Airport in Melrose Park, Illinois.

feed.title: I wore this $7 concealer for 8 hours — it never creased or flaked
feed.summary: The E.l.f. Hydrating Camo Concealer, praised by beauty gurus and customers alike, offers long-lasting, buildable full coverage for just $7. The author, Jess Sims, tested the product for eight hours in the Texas sun and reported no creasing or flaking, noting its creamy texture and matte finish. She uses two shades to highlight and conceal hyperpigmentation, recommending moisturizing beforehand for optimal application.

feed.title: F1 Boom Lures Amazon, Dell and Oracle Into Tech-Sponsor Race
feed.summary: The increasing popularity of Formula One, especially in the U.S., is attracting major tech companies like Amazon, Oracle, and Dell Technologies as sponsors and partners. These partnerships involve using advanced technology for car design, performance optimization, data analysis for fan engagement, and even driver wellness. This trend highlights F1's blend of technological innovation and competitive sport, driving further tech demand.

feed.title: GXO beats Q1 estimates, raises full-year guidance
feed.summary: GXO Logistics Inc. reported better-than-expected first-quarter results, with adjusted diluted earnings of 59 cents per share and a 14% increase in revenue to nearly $2.1 billion. The company raised its full-year guidance, now expecting adjusted diluted EPS between $2.70 and $2.90, and revenue growth of 11% to 15%, driven by solid volume across industries and increased demand for e-commerce outsourcing. These targets do not include the impact of its proposed acquisition of Clipper Logistics plc.

feed.title: Embracing The Inevitable Move From Hardware To Services
feed.summary: Dell Technologies is shifting its focus from hardware sales to software and services, as evidenced by its Dell Technologies World event. The company is expanding its Apex as-a-service portfolio, enhancing its storage software, and building multi-cloud solutions like Project Alpine to offer cloud-like consumption models and address the evolving needs of IT. This strategy aims to provide streamlined experiences, consistent data mobility, and robust cybersecurity solutions for on-premises and public cloud environments.

feed.title: With Amazon approval, what will National Landing mean for the local tech sector?
feed.summary: Amazon's HQ2 approval in National Landing is expected to transform the Arlington, Virginia area into a tech innovation hub, with developer JBG SMITH planning extensive housing, infrastructure, and a 5G-powered smart city. The goal is to attract new companies and talent, creating an environment similar to Kendall Square or South Lake Union, while also addressing local housing needs.

feed.title: Office Depot owner close to decision on sale of retail business as revenue falls
feed.summary: ODP, the owner of Office Depot and OfficeMax, is nearing a decision on the future of its retail business, which could involve a sale or spin-off. This comes as the retail division experienced a 9% decline in first-quarter sales to $943 million, attributed to 114 store closures. Despite the retail challenges, ODP's business-to-business division saw a 9% increase in sales, as the company grapples with ongoing shifts in the office supply market.

feed.title: DevOps: Why it is now the only way to develop software
feed.summary: DevOps is presented as a cultural shift essential for modern software development, moving beyond traditional "silos" and "waterfall" approaches. It emphasizes collaboration between development and operations teams and leverages automation to achieve frequent, seamless updates, meeting high end-user expectations set by major tech companies. The article argues that without DevOps, it's impossible for applications to remain relevant in today's fast-paced digital environment.

feed.title: Seritage Secures Lease with Amazon at The Collection in La Jolla
feed.summary: Seritage Growth Properties and Invesco Real Estate have secured a lease with Amazon for 123,000 square feet at The Collection at UTC in La Jolla. Amazon will occupy the top two floors of the mixed-use project, which includes Class A office, retail, and restaurant space. This expansion is part of Amazon's growing footprint in California, with Seritage CEO Andrea Olshan highlighting the quality and location of the asset.

feed.title: Grocery giant Kroger is almost ready to deliver in Miami. How do you place an order?
feed.summary: Kroger is expanding into South Florida with an online-only grocery delivery service, opening its first spoke facility in Opa-locka by mid-May 2022, with additional locations planned for Broward and Palm Beach counties. The company will not open traditional brick-and-mortar stores, instead operating through a system centered around its Groveland fulfillment center. Customers can place orders via Kroger's website or app, with a delivery fee of $9.95 or free delivery for Boost members, and drivers do not accept tips as they are paid a "great wage."

feed.title: Howard Schultz rolls out wage boost for Starbucks workers as union efforts gain steam
feed.summary: Starbucks interim CEO Howard Schultz announced new worker benefits that would be available only at nonunion stores during his first call with investors since returning to the company's helm. This move comes as union efforts among Starbucks workers continue to gain momentum, and the company has faced multiple NLRB complaints alleging anti-union activities. The announcement is seen as a strategic response to the growing unionization movement within Starbucks.

feed.title: Shopify acquires shipping logistics startup Deliverr for $2.1B
feed.summary: Shopify announced its acquisition of Deliverr, an e-commerce fulfillment startup, for $2.1 billion in cash and stock, marking its largest acquisition to date. This deal aims to create an end-to-end logistics platform for merchants by integrating Deliverr's technology with the Shopify Fulfillment Network. The acquisition will also power Shopify's new "Shop Promise" service, offering two-day and next-day delivery, and is seen as a strategic move to compete with Amazon in the rapidly growing logistics market.

feed.title: BNPL: Affirm to Become First Buy Now, Pay Later Partner “Fully Integrated” to Carat from Fiserv
feed.summary: Affirm and Fiserv have partnered, making Affirm the first Buy Now, Pay Later (BNPL) provider fully integrated into Fiserv's Carat operating system. This collaboration will allow Fiserv's enterprise merchant clients to seamlessly offer Affirm's Adaptive Checkout, providing consumers with flexible payment options. The partnership aims to help merchants attract new customers and boost sales by meeting the growing demand for BNPL services.

feed.title: Quantum computing firm IonQ hit by short seller report
feed.summary: Quantum computing firm IonQ has been targeted by short seller Scorpion Capital, which called the company's claims of having the world's most powerful quantum computer "a hoax" and a "quantum Ponzi scheme." The report prompted a significant drop in IonQ's share price. Despite this, IonQ has garnered investment from major companies like Samsung, Amazon, and Google, and has partnerships with firms such as Hyundai Motor to apply quantum computing to various industries.

feed.title: 2022 Selloff Has Left the U.S. Stock Market Undervalued
feed.summary: The 2022 stock market selloff has pushed the broad U.S. equity market into undervalued territory, trading at a 12% discount to fair value according to Morningstar's equity research. While value stocks remain attractive, growth stocks, particularly small-caps, now offer significant discounts after substantial declines. The article highlights undervalued opportunities in the Communications, Consumer Cyclical, Financial Services, and Technology sectors, despite ongoing headwinds like slowing economic growth, Federal Reserve tightening, rising interest rates, and inflation.

feed.title: A Look At The Exploitation Uber Eats Food Couriers In South Africa Face
feed.summary: This article examines the exploitation faced by Uber Eats food couriers in South Africa, mirroring a global issue within the gig economy. Drivers report significant pay cuts, long arduous hours, and a lack of benefits or support following accidents, contrasting with Uber's claims of prioritizing their well-being. The piece highlights the precarious nature of their "independent contractor" status, advocating for regulation and drawing parallels to a recent UK Supreme Court ruling that reclassified Uber drivers as workers.

feed.title: BREAKING: Arlington landing Boeing corporate headquarters
feed.summary: Aerospace and defense giant Boeing is moving its corporate headquarters from Chicago to Arlington, Virginia. The move brings the company's senior executives closer to government decision-makers in Washington D.C. and includes plans for a new research and technology hub in the area. Virginia officials, including Sen. Mark Warner and Gov. Glenn Youngkin, actively lobbied for the move, highlighting the region's strategic advantages and skilled workforce.

feed.title: Tech sell-off pushes Nasdaq to steepest drop since June 2020
feed.summary: A tech sell-off on Thursday, May 5, 2022 pushed the Nasdaq Composite to its steepest drop since June 2020, wiping out hundreds of billions in market value. This downturn was driven by disappointing earnings reports from cloud and e-commerce companies like Shopify, Amazon, and Meta, coupled with investor concerns following the Federal Reserve's interest rate hike to combat inflation. The rotation out of tech began in late 2021 due to inflation fears and escalated with events like Russia's invasion of Ukraine, leading to significant year-to-date losses for many "Covid winner" stocks.

feed.title: AES announces deals to provide 450 MW of renewable energy to Amazon
feed.summary: The AES Corporation announced two Power Purchase Agreements (PPAs) with Amazon to provide 450 MW of solar and 225 MW of 4-hour battery energy storage. These projects will support Amazon's goal to power its global operations with 100% renewable energy by 2025 and achieve net-zero carbon by 2040. AES has partnered with Fluence for energy storage solutions for one of the projects.

feed.title: Boeing to move headquarters from Chicago to Virginia
authors: David Shepardson and Eric M. Johnson
feed.summary: Boeing announced it will relocate its global headquarters from Chicago to Arlington, Virginia, and establish a new research and technology hub there. This move is intended to improve relationships with customers, federal regulators, and lawmakers, especially following issues with the 737 MAX and other programs. Critics, however, view the frequent relocations as indicative of Boeing prioritizing short-term profits and access to government over engineering excellence.

feed.title: Amazon fires managers at its pro-union New York City warehouse
feed.summary: Amazon fired managers at its JFK8 warehouse in New York City after workers successfully voted to join the Amazon Labor Union (ALU). While Amazon stated the changes were due to evaluating operations and leadership, reports suggest six managers were dismissed because the union won the election. Amazon is currently fighting to overturn the union election results.

feed.title: Ankur Bhatia | CEO | Chogori India Retail Limited
feed.summary: Ankur Bhatia, CEO of Chogori India Retail Limited (CIRL), discusses the sportswear market and Columbia Sportswear's expansion in India. He highlights the company's increasing focus on sourcing from India in line with the "Make in India" initiative and outlines plans to open one store per month in tier 1 and 2 cities. Bhatia also touches upon the global sportswear market growth, the importance of sustainable practices, and the company's strategy to introduce specialized outdoor gear to the Indian market.

feed.title: 7 Charts for Making Sense of These Markets
feed.summary: This article analyzes current market volatility through seven charts, highlighting the Federal Reserve's aggressive interest rate hikes as a primary driver. It discusses the impact on both stock and bond markets, the underperformance of growth stocks versus value stocks, and offers insights on potential opportunities for investors amidst the market adjustments.

feed.title: 20 trustworthy online money-making sites in Kenya in 2026
feed.summary: This article lists 20 trustworthy online platforms where Kenyans can earn money, detailing various opportunities such as freelancing, affiliate marketing, online surveys, and AI training. It provides guidance for beginners on how to get started, emphasizing that many platforms require minimal skills and can lead to significant income with consistent effort. The article also touches on how to earn money specifically via M-Pesa and clarifies which sites are legitimate for making money online in Kenya.

feed.title: The Old Tech FAANG Is Dulled, But a New Version Has Promise
feed.summary: Bank of America strategists have introduced "FAANG 2.0," a new grouping of sectors designed for a world facing inflation, war, and geopolitical shifts, replacing the underperforming original tech FAANG stocks. This new version, comprising fuels, aerospace and defense, agriculture, nuclear and renewables, and gold and metals/minerals, has shown significantly better market performance year to date compared to both the S&P 500 and the original tech FAANG stocks. The article highlights the rationale behind this shift, citing energy security, increased military spending, rising food prices, and gold's role as a refuge asset in the current global climate.

feed.title: Starbucks asks White House for equal time after Biden met with union leaders
feed.summary: Starbucks has requested a meeting with the Biden administration after the White House hosted unionized workers without inviting Starbucks officials, expressing concern that the meeting did not represent the majority of its employees who oppose unionization. This comes as the National Labor Relations Board (NLRB) issued a complaint alleging misconduct by Starbucks against union members, which Starbucks denies. Workers United, representing Starbucks employees, stated they were honored to represent all partners at the White House meeting.

feed.title: AES Corp seals two renewable PPAs with Amazon
feed.summary: The AES Corporation has signed two Power Purchase Agreements (PPAs) with Amazon to deliver renewable energy to the CAISO market. These agreements involve 450MW of solar and 225MW of 4-hour duration battery energy storage projects, helping Amazon achieve its goal of powering global operations with 100% renewable energy by 2025. With these projects, Amazon further solidifies its position as the largest corporate buyer of renewable energy, advancing its commitment to net-zero carbon by 2040.

feed.title: Holy-Moly Mortgage Rates Hit 5.64%, 10-Year Treasury Yield 3.12%, Long-Term Treasury Bond Fund Gets Massacred
feed.summary: Mortgage rates have surged to 5.64%, the highest since 2009, as the 10-year Treasury yield rose to 3.12%. This has led to a significant increase in monthly mortgage payments, impacting housing demand. A long-term Treasury bond ETF has plunged, indicating a "bond massacre" for investors who previously viewed bonds as a conservative investment.

feed.title: 15 Top Cities for Machine Learning Engineer Salaries
feed.summary: This article identifies the top 15 U.S. cities offering the highest salaries for Machine Learning Engineers, based on data from Blind. It highlights that major tech hubs like Silicon Valley and Seattle lead due to high demand from companies like Meta and Apple. The piece also notes the increasing importance and compensation for AI and machine learning skills across industries.

feed.title: Telesat, Globalstar, Intelsat headline upheavals in satellite industry
feed.summary: The satellite communications industry is undergoing significant changes, with major providers like Telesat, Globalstar, and Intelsat experiencing corporate upheavals, new leadership, and project adjustments. These developments underscore the evolving role of satellites in global telecommunications, moving from a relatively minor component to a potentially prominent one due to innovations from companies like OneWeb and SpaceX. These shifts also highlight a broader trend where various companies, including large telecom providers, are

feed.title: Not working out: Peloton plunges after cutting outlook
authors: Mark Gurman and Michael Tobin and Bloomberg
feed.summary: Peloton Interactive Inc. shares tumbled after the company reported a deeper loss than analysts predicted, cut its revenue guidance, and secured a $750 million debt deal. The company, which thrived during the early pandemic, is now facing "softer demand" and continued stock decline despite leadership changes and cost-cutting measures. CEO Barry McCarthy is focused on increasing subscribers and expanding the digital app, while some investors are pushing for a sale of the company amidst its financial struggles.

feed.title: Prologis offers to buy Duke Realty in $23.7 billion deal as warehouse demand soars
feed.summary: Prologis Inc has offered to acquire Duke Realty Corp in an all-stock deal valued at $23.7 billion to capitalize on the surging demand for industrial warehouse space. The offer values Duke at $61.68 per share, representing a 29% premium, as Prologis seeks to maintain its growth amid a tight supply chain and increased e-commerce activity from companies like Amazon.

feed.title: Rackspace is looking to sell itself and exit the public markets, again
feed.summary: Rackspace Technology Inc. is exploring a sale of all or part of its business to return to private ownership, less than two years after re-entering the public market. The company believes a sum-of-the-parts valuation could exceed its current enterprise value, driven by attractive growth in its public cloud sector. This move follows tepid first-quarter financial results, with a net loss of $64 million and modest revenue growth, prompting concerns about its growth trajectory in comparison to the broader cloud market.

feed.title: Intel engineer, running for Congress, mounts union drive at Oregon chip factory
feed.summary: An Intel engineer and congressional candidate, Matt West, is leading a unionization effort for hundreds of his colleagues at Intel's Hillsboro semiconductor factories in Oregon. The drive aims to address issues like long hours, pay disparities, and job security, particularly for engineers working on temporary visas. This initiative comes amidst a broader resurgence of organized labor in the US and during Intel's push for increased domestic chip manufacturing.

feed.title: Google Cloud launches AlloyDB, a PostgreSQL-compatible database for mission-critical workloads
feed.summary: Google Cloud has introduced AlloyDB, a new fully managed, PostgreSQL-compatible relational database service designed for mission-critical workloads. Unveiled at Google I/O, AlloyDB is built on open-source PostgreSQL and Google Cloud's infrastructure, aiming to offer superior performance, scalability, and reliability compared to standard PostgreSQL and AWS Aurora. It emphasizes transparent pricing without I/O charges and includes AI/ML capabilities for management and analytical acceleration, positioning it as a strong competitor to Oracle and AWS in the database market.

feed.title: Rackspace CEO’s comments fuel speculation about another sale of tech company
feed.summary: Rackspace Technology CEO Kevin Jones' recent comments to analysts have sparked speculation about a potential sale or restructuring of the company. Jones indicated that a "sum of the parts valuation" could exceed Rackspace's current enterprise value, leading to considerations of strategic alternatives. While Rackspace later downplayed a full sale, the company is exploring reorganizing its on-premise server and public cloud services into separate entities to "unlock value."

feed.title: Rackspace for sale, looking for privatization
feed.summary: Rackspace Technology, which went public less than two years ago, is seeking privatization due to its market capitalization not reflecting the company's true value. The company, which helps businesses manage cloud environments, needs to make strategic changes to better compete in the growing multicloud market. Although profitable, Rackspace's growth isn't fast enough to satisfy stock market analysts, making privatization an attractive option to allow for necessary repositioning in the market.

feed.title: How Sonos’ new voice assistant could take on Alexa and Google Assistant
feed.summary: Sonos is launching its own voice assistant on June 1, focusing specifically on audio playback, which will support multiple music services. Unlike general-purpose assistants, Sonos Voice Control processes commands on-device for improved privacy and responsiveness. The company believes this specialized approach, combined with new hardware like the Sonos Ray soundbar, can carve out a significant niche in the voice assistant market, especially as adoption for broader smart speakers shows signs of slowing.

feed.title: Summer’s Eve Intimate Skin Care Spa Collection Takes Serum to New Places
feed.summary: Summer's Eve has launched a new "Spa" collection, including an intimate skin serum and a luxurious wash, to elevate daily intimate care routines. The products are formulated with ingredients like vitamin E, aloe, and coconut oil, are pH balanced, gynecologist-tested, and free from dyes, alcohol, and parabens. This launch by Prestige Consumer Healthcare aims to tap into wellness and luxury trends within the intimate care market.
