feed.title: Duke Realty Rejects Nearly $24 Billion Buyout Offer From Prologis
feed.summary: Duke Realty Corp. has rejected a nearly $24 billion buyout offer from warehousing giant Prologis Inc., deeming the unsolicited proposal insufficient. Prologis made its all-stock offer public after more than five months of private overtures. The acquisition would have significantly expanded Prologis's industrial real estate footprint, which already includes over 1 billion square feet used by major e-commerce companies.

feed.title: ReNew Appoints New CFO Also Brings in New General Counsel and Chief Growth Officer
feed.summary: ReNew Power, India’s largest renewable energy company, has announced the appointment of a new Group Chief Financial Officer, Chief Growth Officer, and General Counsel to lead its expansion, including into green hydrogen and other clean energy segments. Kedar Upadhye joins as Group CFO, Vikash Jain as Global General Counsel, and Vikram Kapur as Chief Growth Officer, all bringing extensive experience from various top-tier companies. These strategic hires come as ReNew’s gross portfolio has surged by nearly 20% to 12.1 GW, solidifying its position as India's largest utility-scale solar developer.

feed.title: Global 2000: Berkshire Hathaway Takes Down JPMorgan As America’s Largest Company
feed.summary: Berkshire Hathaway has surpassed JPMorgan Chase to become America's largest public company in the Forbes Global 2000 list, driven by nearly $90 billion in profits. Despite global volatility, U.S. companies like Amazon and ExxonMobil showed significant growth, with Amazon rising to third in the U.S. and ExxonMobil rebounding strongly due to surging energy prices. The article highlights the resilience of top U.S. companies amid inflation and geopolitical challenges.

feed.title: Starbucks Baristas Are Unionizing, and Even Howard Schultz Can’t Make Them Stop
feed.summary: Starbucks baristas are rapidly unionizing, undeterred by the return of longtime CEO Howard Schultz. This movement is inspiring other workers, including those at Amazon, and demonstrates the growing power of organized labor. The article highlights an instance where Schultz's return was met with a mix of corporate welcome and employee activism regarding social issues.

feed.title: Breaking Bad's Giancarlo Esposito Is The Voice Of Sonos' New Alexa-Style Assistant
feed.summary: Sonos has announced a new voice control feature called Sonos Voice Control, launching June 1 in the US. This Alexa-style assistant will be voiced by Giancarlo Esposito, known for his roles in "Breaking Bad" and "The Mandalorian." The company emphasizes that user requests are processed locally and not sent to the cloud, ensuring privacy.

feed.title: Giancarlo Esposito Is the Only Voice AI We'll Ever Need
feed.summary: Giancarlo Esposito, known for his roles in "Breaking Bad" and "Star Wars," is lending his voice to Sonos's new voice control system. This system aims to compete with existing AI companions like Alexa and Google, allowing users to control music and other functions with Esposito's distinct voice. Sonos CEO Patrick Spence describes the collaboration as aiming for natural, unobtrusive, yet confident and engaging voice control, coinciding with the release of the new Sonos Ray soundbar and new color options for the Sonos Roam speaker.

feed.title: Rackspace mulls over business unit sell-off following strategic review of company
feed.summary: Rackspace Technology is considering selling off at least one of its business units following a strategic review that concluded the "sum of its parts" could be more valuable than the company's current form. CEO Kevin Jones stated this decision was influenced by the attractive growth profile of public cloud. The company, which recently announced narrowed losses and a 7% year-on-year revenue rise, plans to reorganize across its distinct public cloud and private cloud/managed hosting markets.

feed.title: How Carter’s is using its Little Planet brand to test sustainability initiatives
feed.summary: Carter's is leveraging its Little Planet brand as an incubator to test new sustainability initiatives, including eco-friendly materials and packaging. This strategy allows the large baby and kidswear retailer to adapt to growing consumer demand for sustainable products without overhauling its entire operation at once. Lessons learned from Little Planet, such as new info tags and recycled product lines, are gradually being integrated into Carter's broader brand portfolio and distributed across various retail partners.

feed.title: Archer Datacenters Partners with Evoque to Expand Nashville Data Center Campus
feed.summary: Archer Datacenters announced a joint venture with Evoque, a Brookfield Infrastructure Partners company, to expand its Nashville Hyperscale campus. This $200 million equity commitment aims to develop critical digital infrastructure across the Nashville and Central Southeast region, providing scaled colocation offerings with rapid delivery and a focus on sustainability. The partnership capitalizes on Nashville's significant economic and population growth, addressing an underserved market with robust power and connectivity solutions, including renewable energy initiatives.

feed.title: USC ISI works with D-Wave to house one of the first U.S-Based Advantage™ Quantum Computers
feed.summary: USC and D-Wave Systems Inc. have launched the first U.S.-based 5,000+ qubit D-Wave quantum computing system at the USC Viterbi School of Engineering’s Information Sciences Institute (ISI). This Advantage™ quantum system, located at the USC-Lockheed Martin Quantum Computing Center, offers academic, government, and business clients access to advanced quantum annealing and hybrid solver services. The system provides a four-fold increase in qubits and enhanced performance, furthering research in quantum simulation, optimization, and machine learning.

feed.title: Realogy rebranding as Anywhere Real Estate
feed.summary: Realogy Holdings Corp. announced at an Investors Day event that it is changing its name to Anywhere Real Estate Inc. The rebranding, which will be complete by the end of the quarter, is part of a larger strategy to invest in advances for consumers demanding a more seamless transaction, without directly affecting its brokerage brands' structure or daily operations. This move follows a strong 2021 and a solid first quarter for Realogy, despite a profit decline, and continued expansion of its iBuying arm.

feed.title: Andy Burke Joins Tishman Speyer to Lead Industrial Platform
feed.summary: Tishman Speyer has appointed Andy Burke as Managing Director, Head of Industrial, to lead its global industrial sector efforts, initially focusing on U.S. acquisition and development opportunities. Burke brings extensive experience from Terreno Realty Corporation, where he managed over 100 industrial transactions valued at over $1.5 billion. This hiring follows Tishman Speyer's recent launch of its industrial property platform and aims to accelerate the firm's growth in this sector.

feed.title: Exclusive-Maker of Walmart, Amazon store-brand baby formulas sees shortages through rest of 2022
feed.summary: Perrigo Company PLC, a major manufacturer of store-brand baby formulas for retailers like Walmart and Amazon, anticipates continued shortages and high demand for the remainder of 2022. The company is operating its facilities at 115% capacity and focusing on specific formulas at the FDA's request, navigating increased pressure on the Biden administration to address the widespread baby formula shortage. This shortage was exacerbated by a significant recall from Abbott Laboratories in February, with Perrigo adjusting production and pricing to meet the surging needs.

feed.title: Starbucks in Grand Rapids votes to unionize — first in Michigan
feed.summary: Workers at a Starbucks store in Grand Rapids have voted to unionize, marking the first Starbucks location in Michigan to do so. This decision is part of a growing national trend for Starbucks employees seeking higher wages and better working conditions. The unionization effort could help rekindle the labor movement in the U.S., especially given Michigan's past as a union stronghold.

feed.title: WD Targets Cloud Challenges
feed.summary: Western Digital (WD) is launching new SSDs and HDDs to address the exponential data growth and performance demands in cloud environments, particularly for hyperscale customers. The company's new 22TB and 26TB UltraSMR HDDs leverage OptiNAND and enhanced SMR technology, while their Ultrastar NVMe PCIe 4.0 SSDs target disaggregated storage in public clouds to improve utilization and density. WD also notes a strong demand for client SSDs driven by remote work and gaming, reinforcing the critical role of storage innovation across the board.

feed.title: Exclusive: Maker of Walmart, Amazon store-brand baby formulas sees shortages through rest of 2022
feed.summary: Perrigo Company PLC, a major producer of store-brand baby formulas for retailers like Walmart and Amazon, anticipates ongoing shortages and heightened demand throughout the remainder of 2022. This scarcity is largely attributed to a significant recall by Abbott Laboratories in February. Perrigo's manufacturing facilities are operating at 115% capacity, and the company is collaborating with retailers to ensure weekly stock allocations.

feed.title: Sonos Ray vs Beam (Gen 2) vs Sonos Arc: Which soundbar is best for you?
feed.summary: This article compares Sonos' three soundbar models: the Ray, Beam (Gen 2), and Arc, to help consumers choose the best option for their needs. It details the differences in design, connectivity, sound capabilities (including Dolby Atmos support), and smart features. The article highlights price points and suggests which soundbar is best suited for various TV sizes and desired audio experiences, from basic TV audio enhancement to immersive home cinema.

feed.title: A Look Into Public Clouds From the Ransomware Actor's Perspective
feed.summary: This article examines the potential evolution of ransomware attacks in public cloud environments, proposing that while traditional ransomware is largely ineffective, threat actors could adapt their tactics, techniques, and procedures (TTPs) to be cloud-native. It discusses how attackers might gain initial access, execute attacks through control and data plane APIs, and achieve privilege escalation using IAM misconfigurations. The article concludes that public clouds are inherently more resilient to ransomware than on-premises systems, but emphasizes the need for organizations to proactively secure identities and adopt best practices to mitigate theoretical cloud-based ransomware threats.

feed.title: QVC in the digital age: Tech giants like YouTube embrace livestream shopping
feed.summary: Tech giants like YouTube are embracing livestream shopping, reimagining the QVC model from the 1990s. YouTube aims to streamline the existing organic behavior of users seeking product reviews on its platform by integrating live video shopping experiences with influencers. This move comes as livestream shopping has become a multi-billion dollar industry, particularly significant in China, and presents a win-win opportunity for creators and viewers by making the process easier and more interactive.

feed.title: Starbucks to add abortion travel coverage to U.S. health benefits
feed.summary: Starbucks Corp announced it will reimburse U.S. employees for travel expenses if they need to go more than 100 miles from home to obtain an abortion. This decision follows a leaked Supreme Court draft opinion that suggests Roe v. Wade could be overturned, leading to tighter abortion restrictions in some states. Starbucks joins other major companies like Amazon and Microsoft in offering similar benefits.

feed.title: The PG 100: Ranking Top Food Retailers in North America
feed.summary: The "PG 100" report ranks the top 100 food retailers in North America, highlighting an 11% increase in combined sales to $2.275 trillion in 2021. The report discusses challenges and benefits faced by retailers due to COVID-19 and rising fuel prices, as well as significant merger and acquisition activity in the industry. It provides a detailed table with sales, store counts, and top executives for each of the ranked companies.

feed.title: Starbucks to cover employees’ travel expenses for abortions; gender surgeries
feed.summary: Starbucks announced an expansion of its health care benefits to cover travel expenses for employees seeking abortions or gender-affirming procedures if these services are not available within 100 miles of their homes. This decision comes in the wake of a leaked draft U.S. Supreme Court opinion potentially overturning Roe v. Wade, with the company affirming its commitment to ensuring employee access to quality healthcare. Starbucks joins other major companies in offering this benefit, consistent with its history of advocating for liberal causes.

feed.title: Amazon’s unpaid time off practices violate USERRA, class-action suit claims
feed.summary: A class-action lawsuit alleges that Amazon discriminated against military service members by counting military leave as unpaid time off (UTO), leading to negative UTO balances and subsequent termination. The plaintiff, a former Alabama Army National Guard member, claims Amazon violated the Uniformed Services Employment and Reemployment Rights Act (USERRA) when she was fired after taking military leave. USERRA prohibits employers from denying employment benefits or retention based on military service and generally requires comparable benefits for military and non-military leaves.

feed.title: Why unattended retail is exploding in response to consumer acceptance
feed.summary: The article discusses the rapid expansion of unattended retail due to growing consumer acceptance, driven by a desire for control and comfort in transactions. It highlights how new technologies and service concepts are emerging in various locations like sports arenas and healthcare facilities. Experts from PepsiCo, Canteen Vending Services, Aramark, and Maumee Valley Group weigh in on the opportunities and challenges, including collaboration with food delivery services and the evolving role of traditional vending operators.

feed.title: Netflix lays off 150 employees as the streaming service contends with big subscriber losses
feed.summary: Netflix is laying off approximately 150 employees, less than 2% of its 11,000 staffers, primarily in the U.S., due to slowing revenue growth. This move comes less than a month after the streaming service reported its first subscriber loss in a decade and saw its stock value drop significantly. The company is exploring new strategies like lower-priced, ad-supported tiers and cracking down on password sharing to regain subscribers.

feed.title: Starbucks Labor Controversy Sparks Discussion About Unionizing and Company Reputation
feed.summary: Starbucks is facing a labor controversy with Starbucks Workers United, which has filed numerous unfair labor practice charges against the company for allegedly interfering with unionization efforts. This situation has sparked a broader discussion about company reputation and the historical context of labor relations, with experts like Robert Josephson highlighting the importance of companies addressing employee concerns to avoid reputational damage. The article suggests that genuine empathy from leadership and effective communication can bridge the gap between management and employees in such disputes.

feed.title: Amazon, Kong Studios Opening Offices In Santa Monica
feed.summary: Amazon and game developer Kong Studios Inc. are establishing new offices in Santa Monica, a move city officials expect to bolster the local workforce and expand technology, game development, and corporate job opportunities. Amazon plans to open a "tech hub" in mid-2023, bringing over 1,000 new tech and corporate jobs to Santa Monica, while Kong Studios is relocating its headquarters to the city. This expansion is seen as a positive sign for Santa Monica's economic growth and its strong technology sector.

feed.title: The Most Innovative and Important People in DC’s Tech Scene
feed.summary: This article identifies 225 innovative and important figures in the DC tech scene across various categories including entrepreneurs, government officials, cybersecurity experts, and venture capitalists. It highlights the unique trajectory of the region's tech industry, which is deeply rooted in government but constantly evolving and expanding. The piece details key individuals and companies that are shaping the technological landscape in Washington, D.C.

feed.title: JD.com Opens First Overseas Service Centers in the US
feed.summary: JD.com has opened two new overseas service centers in Los Angeles and New Jersey, marking its first such venture in the overseas market. These centers will offer comprehensive aftersales and maintenance services for electronics and appliances, supported by JD's air cargo lines and self-operated warehouses in the US. The initiative aims to provide end-to-end supply chain logistics services and reduce repair times for brands and cross-border merchants.

feed.title: US stocks suffer biggest daily drop in almost two years
feed.summary: US stocks experienced their largest daily decline in nearly two years, as inflation concerns and the prospect of stricter monetary policy weighed on markets. The S&P 500 dropped 4%, with consumer shares plummeting over 6%, led by Target's steep fall after a reduced profit forecast. Growing hawkish sentiment from the Federal Reserve, global supply chain issues, and geopolitical tensions continue to fuel investor anxiety.

feed.title: Goodbye, Gig Economy. It’s a Multi-Earner Era
feed.summary: The gig economy is evolving into a "multi-earner era" driven by platforms that enable individuals to generate income beyond traditional employment. This trend has significant implications for workers, employers, and the economy, with younger generations like Gen Z actively participating in various "X-to-Earn" verticals. Employers face challenges in hiring and retention as workers seek multiple income streams, potentially requiring increased flexibility and competitive wages to attract and retain talent.

feed.title: Netgear Orbi 6E Mesh review: A powerful—and expensive—Wi-Fi mesh system
feed.summary: The Netgear Orbi 6E Mesh system offers extremely high throughput, especially on the 6GHz band, and generally performs very well, particularly for homes with many smart devices. However, its significant price tag of $1,500 for a three-pack and its reliance on paid subscriptions for desirable features like parental controls and extended tech support temper its overall appeal. While it outperforms competitors in 6GHz speeds, its value proposition is diminished by these additional costs, making it most suitable for users prioritizing top-tier performance over budget.

feed.title: Why S&P booted Tesla from its ESG index
feed.summary: S&P Dow Jones Indices removed Tesla from its S&P 500 ESG Index due to a decline in its ESG rank compared to global peers. Despite Tesla's role in the transition to electric vehicles, the decision was influenced by claims of racial discrimination, poor working conditions at its factory, and its handling of a federal investigation into autopilot-related deaths. Elon Musk called ESG an "outrageous scam" in response to the decision.

feed.title: Target Shares Plunge, Drags Down Consumer Sector ETFs
feed.summary: Target Corp. shares plummeted after missing quarterly earnings forecasts and warning of higher costs, dragging down consumer sector exchange-traded funds. The retailer attributed the profit decline to unexpected fuel and freight costs and reiterated its commitment not to pass these costs onto consumers in the long term. This downturn also reflects a broader shift in consumer spending from goods back towards services in a post-Covid-19 world.

feed.title: Wall Street ends sharply lower as Target and growth stocks sink
feed.summary: Wall Street closed sharply lower on Wednesday after Target's stock plummeted by about a quarter of its value, exposing concerns about the U.S. economy due to surging prices. This marked the worst one-day loss for the S&P 500 and Dow Jones Industrial Average since June 2020, as inflation continued to erode consumer purchasing power, impacting retailers and prompting a market sell-off. Megacap growth stocks also contributed to the decline, with the Nasdaq falling significantly, amidst broader economic worries including rising inflation, supply chain issues, and central bank tightening.

feed.title: American Makes Microsoft Azure Preferred Cloud Provider for Airline Applications
feed.summary: American Airlines has chosen Microsoft Azure as its preferred cloud platform for various airline applications, including airport taxiing decisions and managing operational data. This move follows previous partnerships with IBM, and American Airlines aims to leverage Azure's AI, machine learning, and data analytics to optimize customer experience and operations, particularly for gating decisions at its DFW hub. This decision positions American Airlines among other major U.S. carriers embracing cloud-first approaches for future resilience and innovation.

feed.title: Kroger VP of Shared Services Jamie Lancaster to Present on Loyalty at Analytics Unite 2022
feed.summary: Jamie Lancaster, VP of Shared Services at Kroger, is scheduled to present on customer loyalty at the Analytics Unite: The Summit for Retail and Consumer Brands event, taking place from June 21-23 at the Drake Hotel in Chicago. He will discuss leveraging valuable behavioral insights from loyal customers to inform various areas of the organization. Lancaster, who leads Kroger's customer contact center and support services, will be joined by Josh Blacksmith of Kimberly-Clark.

feed.title: FedEx expands pilot of self-driving trucks
feed.summary: FedEx is expanding its pilot program for self-driving trucks by adding a new commercial lane in Texas, collaborating with Aurora Innovation Inc. This expansion is part of FedEx's strategy to compete with Amazon in autonomous cargo hauling, following successful earlier pilots that completed 60,000 miles with zero safety incidents. The company is actively integrating autonomous technology into its operations to enhance efficiency and meet growing customer demand.

feed.title: D-Market Elektronik Hizmetler ve Ticaret (Nasdaq:HEPS) - Stock Analysis
feed.summary: This analysis of D-Market Elektronik Hizmetler ve Ticaret (Nasdaq:HEPS) from Simply Wall St provides a detailed overview including valuation, growth forecasts, past performance, financial health, and dividend information. The report highlights that HEPS is trading significantly below its estimated fair value with projected revenue growth, despite facing a forecast decline in earnings and current unprofitability. Key takeaways point to expanded delivery services and strategic partnerships as drivers for future success, while also noting challenges from intensifying competition and macroeconomic volatility.

feed.title: Will smart shopping carts transform the shopping experience at Albertsons?
feed.summary: Albertsons is expanding its pilot program for smart shopping carts, manufactured by Veeve, across several dozen stores after successful initial tests in California and Idaho. These carts allow customers to complete their shopping and checkout without needing a traditional register, aiming to enhance the grocery experience through technology. While the concept offers convenience, industry experts and commentators raise concerns about the high cost of implementation, potential user adoption challenges, and whether such advanced technology distracts from fundamental store operational improvements.

feed.title: Broadcom in Talks to Acquire VMware, the Cloud Computing Company (Published 2022)
feed.summary: Broadcom, a semiconductor giant, is reportedly in discussions to acquire VMware, a cloud computing company known for its virtualization software. This potential acquisition would expand Broadcom's presence in cloud computing and continue CEO Hock E. Tan's strategy of diversifying beyond chip companies following a blocked deal with Qualcomm in 2018. Following the news, VMware's stock saw a significant increase, while Broadcom's shares experienced a slight dip.

feed.title: Amazon (AMZN) Announces New Fire 7 Tablets
feed.summary: Amazon has announced its new Fire 7 and Fire 7 Kids tablets, which are available for pre-order and will start shipping on June 29, 2022. These tablets serve as budget-friendly alternatives to the Apple iPad mini, with prices starting at $59.99 and $109.99 respectively. The new Fire 7 boasts significant upgrades in battery life, RAM, and responsiveness compared to its 2019 predecessor, while only increasing in price by $10.

feed.title: Edgewell Unveils New Skin Care Brand
feed.summary: Edgewell Personal Care, known for Jack Black, is launching a new genderless skin care brand called Fieldtrip on June 6. This in-house developed brand targets Gen Z and Millennial consumers with vegan, cruelty-free products ranging from $13 to $21, emphasizing sustainability and broad appeal. Fieldtrip is expected to achieve $4 million in retail sales in its first year and will be available on its website, Nordstrom, Nordstrom Rack, Amazon, and Macy's.

feed.title: ARKO Corp. Earns Spot on Fortune 500 List
feed.summary: ARKO Corp., the parent company of GPM Investments, has been named to the 2022 Fortune 500 list, ranking No. 498 with over $6 billion in revenues. This marks ARKO's first appearance on the list, demonstrating significant growth and successful acquisition strategies since joining NASDAQ. Other convenience store operators like Murphy USA Inc., Casey's General Stores Inc., and TravelCenters of America Inc. also made the list.

feed.title: Omnicom’s new supply chain tool adjusts media spend based on inventory
feed.summary: Omnicom Media Group (OMG) has launched the Supply Chain IQ Score, a new tool designed to connect media spend with product availability. This tool uses data from over 80% of top U.S. retailers to help marketers adjust media investments based on physical, digital, and in-transit SKU inventory. The goal is to optimize media spend amid ongoing supply chain disruptions, allowing brands to shift focus to products with healthy inventory and high sales correlation, thereby improving ROI and meeting performance goals.

feed.title: Amazon gains on UPS in package delivery volume
feed.summary: Amazon's package delivery business, Amazon Logistics, is rapidly gaining on UPS in terms of delivery volume, having already surpassed FedEx in 2020. While Amazon Logistics held a 22% share of the parcel delivery market by volume last year, its revenue share is significantly lower at 12% due to its Prime free shipping model. Amazon plans to invest $1 billion in other logistics companies to further its growth.

feed.title: Interxion pauses plans for $300 million expansion in Dublin
feed.summary: Interxion has paused a $300 million expansion plan in Dublin due to a de facto moratorium placed on new data center developments in the greater Dublin area by EirGrid, Ireland's national grid operator. This moratorium, which could last until 2028, has led to calls for a nationwide ban and has prompted criticism from various industry bodies, despite local council efforts to prevent further data center construction. The situation highlights the growing pressure on Ireland's energy resources from data centers, which now consume 11 percent of the country's total grid-generated electricity.

feed.title: Cleveland-Cliffs and TravelCenters of America return to Fortune 500
feed.summary: Cleveland-Cliffs and TravelCenters of America have rejoined the Fortune 500 list. Walmart topped the overall list, followed by Amazon and Apple. The article also mentions other related business news.

feed.title: Pitney Bowes Parcel Shipping Index Finds US Parcel Volume Reached Record High of 21.5 Billion in 2021
feed.summary: The Pitney Bowes Parcel Shipping Index revealed that US parcel volume grew by six percent in 2021, reaching a record high of 21.5 billion parcels. Carrier revenues also increased significantly to $188 billion, up 16 percent from 2020. The report highlights the continued impact of the pandemic on shipping and logistics, forecasting further growth to 25-40 billion parcels by 2027.

feed.title: Amazon.com Inc. delays hiring by months at new 1 million-square-foot facility in Clarksville
feed.summary: Amazon.com Inc. has delayed hiring for its new 1 million-square-foot fulfillment center in Clarksville, Tennessee. The company is reportedly waiting to invest in manpower until there is a clear inbound supply of materials for the facility. This delay indicates a revised hiring schedule compared to initial plans.

feed.title: Broadcom Inc in talks to acquire VMware: sources
feed.summary: Broadcom Inc. is reportedly in discussions to acquire cloud-computing company VMware Inc., a deal that would significantly expand the chipmaker's software presence. This potential acquisition aligns with CEO Hock Tan's strategy of diversifying Broadcom through software companies. VMware, valued at around US$40 billion, would provide Broadcom with greater access to the data center market, a critical area for growth.

feed.title: Caterpillar To Expand Texas Manufacturing Facility
feed.summary: Caterpillar Inc. is expanding its manufacturing plant in Schertz, Texas, with a $24 million investment in new equipment and the addition of 24 new jobs by 2026. This expansion will bring the total workforce to 169 jobs and a payroll exceeding $8 million, supported by a 10-year agreement with the Schertz Economic Development Corporation. The facility specializes in machining engine components for various Caterpillar products, reinforcing the company's commitment to the region.

feed.title: How Amazon, Microsoft, Costco and more Seattle-area brands rank by reputation
feed.summary: Amazon ranked highest among Seattle-area companies in a recent Axios and Harris Poll survey assessing the reputations of the 100 most visible corporate brands in the U.S. Conversely, Costco, based in Issaquah, experienced a 17-place drop in the same survey. The article highlights how local companies performed in this national reputational ranking.

feed.title: Walmart Expanding Drone Delivery Network to Six States
feed.summary: Walmart is expanding its drone delivery network to serve approximately 4 million households across six states: Arizona, Arkansas, Florida, Texas, Utah, and Virginia. This initiative aims to compete with companies like Amazon and FedEx in the growing speedy delivery market. The service will deliver packages up to 10 pounds within 30 minutes for a $3.99 fee and projects over 1 million drone deliveries annually.

feed.title: UGA honors companies that hired the most UGA grads
feed.summary: The University of Georgia recognized the top 25 employers of its Class of 2021 at an event in Sanford Stadium. These companies hired graduates across various industries, from technology and finance to retail and healthcare. UGA's Career Center provides resources for employers to connect with its diverse talent pool.

feed.title: Our verdict on the Garmin Instinct 2S GPS smartwatch
feed.summary: This review covers the Garmin Instinct 2S Solar smartwatch, highlighting its robust features, impressive battery life (especially the solar model), and comprehensive health and fitness tracking capabilities. The article notes its affordability compared to other high-end Garmin watches, praising its utility for keen runners and triathletes despite some limitations in music storage and advanced mapping.

feed.title: Kroger Extends Its Delivery Reach in Ohio
feed.summary: Kroger is expanding its delivery network in Ohio with a new 61,000-square-foot facility in Lockbourne, powered by Ocado Group technology. This "spoke" facility will serve central Ohio and act as a last-mile cross-dock location, extending delivery services up to 200 miles. The expansion is expected to create 200 jobs and further Kroger's digital shopping experience, including the Boost by Kroger Plus service for customers.

feed.title: Zadara edge cloud surpasses 400 points of presence
feed.summary: Zadara, an edge cloud provider, has expanded its global presence to over 400 points of presence across 24 countries, partnering with more than 250 managed service providers. Despite falling short of its 2020 target of 1,000 locations by the end of 2021, the company claims to have more edge points of presence than other public clouds. Zadara offers compute, storage, and networking as managed services and has seen significant growth in revenue and customers, funding its expansion through its own revenues and over $60 million in venture funding.

feed.title: After worst financial quarter in years, Amazon puts plans for large distribution center in Round Rock on hold
feed.summary: Amazon has decided to put plans for a large distribution center in Round Rock, near Austin, on hold. This decision comes after the e-commerce giant experienced its worst financial quarter in years and is looking to shrink its nationwide warehouse footprint. The move has local implications for the Austin area.

feed.title: 100-megawatt Sunflower solar station unveiled in Mississippi Delta
feed.summary: Entergy Mississippi unveiled the 100-megawatt Sunflower Solar Station, the state's largest solar power plant, in Sunflower County. This facility will power 16,000 homes and is the first step in Entergy's plan to add 1,000 megawatts of renewable energy over the next five years. The project highlights collaboration with Mississippi businesses and provides clean energy while offering a hedge against rising natural gas prices.

feed.title: Hyperion looks to slower growth for a helping hand
feed.summary: Australia's largest growth manager, Hyperion, is betting on a counterintuitive outcome—an economic downturn and anemic growth—to revive its performance. Despite a 36% year-to-date loss, Hyperion's CIO Mark Arnold believes that high inflation and high interest rates are temporary and will retreat as the economy cools, providing a tailwind for growth stocks. The firm argues that its disruptive holdings, like Tesla and Amazon, will outperform in a cooler economy where growth is scarce, forcing capital allocators to invest in companies with double-digit earnings growth.

feed.title: Courts Are Not A Weapon: How Corporations Like Chevron Use The Law To Get Their Way
feed.summary: This article discusses how corporations like Chevron weaponize legal systems against activists and critics, exemplified by the case of Steven Donziger. It highlights the extensive legal battle between Chevron and Donziger, who secured a $9.5 billion settlement for environmental destruction in Ecuador, and details the subsequent corporate retaliation he faced. The piece advocates for shareholders, investors, and governments to promote corporate social responsibility and prevent the misuse of legal processes to suppress dissent, emphasizing a zero-tolerance approach to retaliation against human rights defenders.

feed.title: Coty launches first-ever Chloé Fragrances e-commerce store
feed.summary: Coty Inc. has launched the first-ever Chloé Fragrances digital store in partnership with e-commerce platform Lazada. The digital store, hosted on LazMall Prestige, will feature Chloé Signature and Nomade lines, along with exclusive launch sets and will be supported by a digital marketing campaign and a live stream event. This move is part of Coty's strategy to expand its premium digital footprint across Southeast Asia, leveraging the growth in luxury e-commerce.

feed.title: Tech Moves: Elizabeth Scallon departs Amazon for HP; Fauna hires marketing exec; and more
feed.summary: Elizabeth Scallon, a Seattle tech veteran from Amazon, has moved to HP as director of Incubation enablement. Fauna has hired John Novak as vice president of marketing, and Blueprint Technologies brought on Gary McMath as chief of growth. Several other tech companies, including NAVEX and Unbounce, also announced significant personnel changes across leadership roles in the Pacific Northwest tech community.

feed.title: Broadcom will tame the VMware beast
feed.summary: Broadcom's planned acquisition of VMware for $61 billion signifies a new era for the virtualization leader, focusing on financial performance and shareholder value. The article details Broadcom's strategy of optimizing profitability by focusing on recurring revenue, cutting R&D and sales/marketing expenses for less profitable areas, and standardizing G&A. For customers, this likely means higher prices and a more focused product portfolio, with core offerings like vSphere being emphasized while less profitable or unproven ventures like Project Monterey face scrutiny.

feed.title: Putting Recent Market Volatility in Perspective
feed.summary: This article provides perspective on recent market volatility, noting that while 2022 has been a bumpy ride for investors with significant downturns in growth stocks and technology, such fluctuations are not historically uncommon. It examines the CBOE VIX Index and standard deviation data to show increased volatility, driven by inflation fears and rising interest rates, but emphasizes that market losses are a normal part of investing. The piece concludes by advising long-term investors to maintain their asset mix and avoid drastic changes unless retirement or significant near-term expenses necessitate a re-evaluation of their portfolio.

feed.title: How Chatbots are Revolutionizing Customer Experience
feed.summary: Modern AI-powered chatbots are transforming customer experience by handling various tasks from ordering taxis to booking appointments, driven by advancements in AI, Machine Learning, and Natural Language Processing (NLP). Unlike traditional rule-based bots, NLP allows chatbots to understand complex conversations, retain context, and interpret human sentiment by integrating with external knowledge sources. Conversational AI, built on neural networks, enables chatbots to learn and improve continuously, process vast amounts of unstructured data to predict user behavior, and perform repetitive tasks, making them indispensable for businesses and freeing up human employees for more complex issues.

feed.title: GM steals executive back from Amazon to lead global workplace safety
feed.summary: General Motors has appointed Marcos Purty as its new vice president of Global Workplace Safety, replacing the retiring Jim Glynn. Purty returns to GM from Amazon, bringing 25 years of prior experience with GM, including various leadership roles in manufacturing and strategy. His critical mandate will be to enhance workplace safety across all GM facilities and to support the company's transformation towards all-electric vehicles and carbon neutrality.

feed.title: Five Below opening location in East Setauket this summer
feed.summary: Five Below is set to open a new store in East Setauket on July 1st, located in the Suffolk Plaza shopping center. The store will occupy approximately 20,000 square feet next to a future Amazon Fresh, in a space previously housing a Waldbaum’s grocery store. This new location will bring low-cost products to the community and is also hiring staff.

feed.title: Moderna CEO Joins List of Billionaires Committed to Philanthropy
feed.summary: Moderna CEO Stéphane Bancel announced his plan to exercise 4.59 million stock options and donate the estimated $355 million in proceeds to charity, a process expected to take about a year. He cited a Jesuit background and the principle of servant leadership as motivations, and his intentions align with other billionaires like MacKenzie Scott, Bill Gates, and Warren Buffett who have pledged significant portions of their fortunes to philanthropy. Bancel emphasized transparency regarding these sales and confirmed he will be using a trading plan to mitigate impact on Moderna's stock price.

feed.title: Boeing will move global HQ to Arlington
feed.summary: Boeing announced its decision to relocate its global headquarters from Chicago to its existing campus in Arlington, Virginia. This move will make Boeing the largest defense contractor headquartered in Virginia, leveraging its proximity to government stakeholders and a skilled workforce. The company also plans to develop a research and technology hub in Arlington, supported by a significant gift to Virginia Tech.

feed.title: Industry backs Lloyd’s of London’s $465m DXC Technology contract extension
feed.summary: The insurance industry has largely welcomed Lloyd’s of London's $465 million contract extension with DXC Technology, viewing it as a crucial step towards digital transformation. This agreement aims to modernize Lloyd's IT systems by transitioning around 400 London market insurance companies to a cloud-native digital platform running on Amazon Web Services. This move is expected to significantly improve speed, efficiency, and operational resilience, transforming the market from a paper-based system to a data-focused, automated, and cost-efficient one.

feed.title: iRobot Unveils iRobot OS - The Most Thoughtfully Intelligent Operating System for the Home
feed.summary: iRobot has launched iRobot OS, a new operating system that enhances the intelligence of its home robots. This OS integrates advanced computer vision and machine learning to offer features like improved pet-centric cleaning, object avoidance, and enhanced voice command capabilities for Roomba j7 and j7+ robot vacuums. iRobot OS is designed to make robot cleaning more effective and adapt to user preferences and home environments.

feed.title: American Eagle’s Quiet Platforms partners with global shipper Pitney Bowes
feed.summary: American Eagle's logistics platform, Quiet Platforms, has partnered with global shipper Pitney Bowes to enhance its delivery and fulfillment capabilities. This collaboration aims to offer faster delivery services and logistics to its network of retailers and brands, strengthening Quiet Platforms' position as an "anti-Amazon" open-sharing logistics model. The partnership will leverage Pitney Bowes' Designed Delivery service to customize delivery networks for Quiet Platforms' clients like Steve Madden, Kohl’s, and Peloton.

feed.title: ZIM Logistics China (ZLC), Ladingo and ZIM Announce the Launch of ZL MAX™ - a New Service Package for Amazon Sellers and eCommerce Businesses
feed.summary: ZIM Logistics China (ZLC), Ladingo, and ZIM Integrated Shipping Services have partnered to launch ZL MAX™, a new comprehensive service package designed for Amazon sellers and eCommerce businesses operating on the China-US West Coast trade route. This service provides end-to-end logistics, including a dedicated digital platform from Ladingo for instant quotes and LCL shipment booking, and leverages ZIM's eCommerce Xpress Service for fast transit times. The collaboration aims to offer reliable, digital, and efficient cross-border shipping solutions amidst growing eCommerce demand and supply chain challenges.

feed.title: XDAT Holdings See Big Achievements
feed.summary: Franklin Exponential Data ETF (XDAT) holdings Fortinet, Datadog Inc., and ZoomInfo have recently announced new achievements or offerings. Fortinet launched FortiNDR for enhanced cybersecurity, Datadog achieved AWS Education Competency, and ZoomInfo's data is now available in its Chorus platform. These developments are expected to impact the actively managed XDAT fund, which invests in companies benefiting from the growth and use of large datasets.

feed.title: ADM’s flaxseed products ship globally
feed.summary: The Archer-Daniels-Midland (ADM) plant in Red Wing, Minnesota, which began as Zumbro Linseed Company in 1902, continues to process flaxseed for global distribution. ADM, also founded in 1902, acquired the Red Wing facility in 1971, making it the company's last remaining flaxseed processing plant. The article details how flaxseed oil is used in industrial applications, supplements, and increasingly in human consumption, with the Red Wing team selling products like "Linsheen" and "Knwble Grwn" online.

feed.title: Kroger to extend greater Columbus home delivery reach with Lockbourne facility
feed.summary: Kroger has opened a new 61,000-square-foot delivery hub in Lockbourne, near Rickenbacker International Airport, to expand its home delivery services in greater Columbus and surrounding areas. This facility will serve customers up to 200 miles away in over 250 ZIP codes and expects to employ up to 200 workers. The move enhances Kroger's delivery capabilities, with its own associates handling deliveries, and represents an extension of its partnership with U.K.-based e-commerce company Ocado.

feed.title: Quantrepreneurs: Wall Street Quants Who Left Trading to Build Startups
feed.summary: This article profiles eight "quantrepreneurs"—quantitative finance professionals who transitioned from lucrative Wall Street trading careers at firms like Citadel and Renaissance Technologies to found or join tech startups. Inspired by Jeff Bezos, these individuals sought more impactful work, moving into diverse fields such as AI in insurance, medical technology, sustainable energy, decentralized finance, and real estate tech. Their stories highlight a growing trend of quants applying their analytical skills to real-world problems, often leveraging non-compete periods to explore entrepreneurial ventures.

feed.title: To Promote 'Stranger Things,' These Businesses Developed an App That Lets You Order a Pizza With Your Mind
feed.summary: To promote the fourth season of Netflix's "Stranger Things," Domino's partnered with WorkInProgress and Unit9 to launch a new "mind-ordering" app. This app allows users to order pizza using head movements, mimicking the telekinetic powers of the character Eleven. It also features a "Just for Fun" mode to explore the show's world and discover Easter eggs, building on Domino's history of innovative ordering methods.

feed.title: Walmart is using its thousands of stores to battle Amazon for e-commerce market share
feed.summary: Walmart is leveraging its extensive network of nearly 4,700 stores across the U.S. as "shoppable fulfillment centers" to boost its e-commerce market share and compete with Amazon. The retailer is transforming its physical locations into hubs for drone deliveries, automated online grocery order fulfillment, and direct-to-fridge drop-offs, aiming to provide faster and more efficient service. This strategy also involves wooing third-party sellers by offering fulfillment services from its stores and expanding its delivery and membership programs like GoLocal and Walmart+.

feed.title: Amazon CEO Andy Jassy earned 6,474 times the median Amazon employee’s salary
feed.summary: Amazon CEO Andy Jassy received a compensation package of nearly $213 million in 2021, which was 6,474 times the median Amazon employee's salary of $32,855. This high compensation was primarily due to a special restricted stock award tied to his promotion to CEO. While several other Fortune 500 CEOs also earned significantly more than their median employees, Jassy's ratio was exceptionally high, sparking controversy among shareholder advisory firms.

feed.title: Amazon consumer CEO Dave Clark resigns
feed.summary: Dave Clark, Amazon's consumer CEO, has resigned after 23 years with the company, effective July 1. His departure signals potential changes in the consumer division, which faced challenges with overbuilt warehouse space and a weak profit outlook. CEO Andy Jassy acknowledged the need for further improvements and will announce a succession plan in the coming weeks.

feed.title: Investing in Big Data with Data Center REITs
feed.summary: This article explores the concept of investing in data center Real Estate Investment Trusts (REITs) as a way to gain exposure to the big data sector. While acknowledging the appeal of REITs for diversification and income, the authors argue that data center REITs carry significant risks, resembling tech stocks more than traditional real estate investments. They conclude that such REITs offer too much risk without sufficient upside potential, suggesting alternative investments like NVIDIA for data center growth exposure.

feed.title: Get a TCL Roku Smart TV for $100 during Walmart+ Weekend
feed.summary: Walmart+ Weekend is offering a 32-inch TCL Roku Smart TV for just $100. This budget-friendly TV includes features like 720p HD resolution, access to numerous streaming services via Roku, voice control, and an ARC HDMI port, making it a solid deal for those looking for an affordable smart TV. The deal is available until June 5th for Walmart+ members.

feed.title: What Does Amazon's Stock Split Mean for Investors?
feed.summary: Amazon is executing a 20-1 stock split, its first in over two decades, effective June 3. The split will adjust Morningstar's fair value estimate for Amazon to $192 per share from $3,850, but senior analyst Dan Romanoff's long-term view remains unchanged, anticipating continued growth in e-commerce, AWS, and advertising. Other major tech companies like Alphabet and Tesla are also planning stock splits.

feed.title: Teresa Carlson returns to Microsoft
feed.summary: Teresa Carlson has rejoined Microsoft as a corporate Vice President and executive-in-residence, nearly 12 years after her previous departure. Carlson, a prominent figure in government cloud computing, left Amazon Web Services where she led their public sector growth, and then had a brief stint as chief growth officer at Splunk before her recent move back to Microsoft. Her return marks a significant development in her career trajectory within the technology industry.

feed.title: Amazon executive behind its massive delivery operation to leave after 23 years
feed.summary: Dave Clark, the Amazon executive responsible for building its vast delivery network, is stepping down as CEO of the company's consumer business after 23 years. His departure signifies a shift in Amazon's leadership following Jeff Bezos's exit and comes as the company faces economic challenges, including a recent $2 billion hit from overbuilt warehousing and transportation capacity. Clark, known for taking risks like acquiring planes and championing warehouse robots, indicated he wants to return to "building" and leaves Amazon with a plan to address inflationary challenges.

feed.title: Ford Motor Company Will Start Online, Fixed-Price, No Haggle Sales For EVs (Updated with Video!)
feed.summary: Ford CEO Jim Farley announced that the company will transition to 100% online, fixed-price sales for its electric vehicles, including direct delivery to customers' homes. This move aims to bypass the traditional dealership experience and excessive markups, following a model similar to Tesla and drawing inspiration from companies like Target and Amazon. While dealerships will still exist, they will need to adapt to this new online-focused, no-haggle sales approach for EVs, with potential expansion to all vehicle sales if successful.

feed.title: Toxic Products Sold at Dollar Stores
feed.summary: A report by the Campaign for Healthier Solutions reveals that over half of products tested from dollar stores like Family Dollar, Dollar General, and Five Below contain hazardous chemicals. These toxic products, some targeted at children, include substances like lead, phthalates, PVC, BPAs, and PFAS, which are linked to various health issues. The article lists 30 specific toxic products found in dollar stores, ranging from children's headphones and toys to food packaging and cooking pans.

feed.title: Edgewell Personal Care Announces Gen-Z Focused Clean Skincare Brand
feed.summary: Edgewell Personal Care has launched Fieldtrip, a new unisex clean skincare brand aimed at Gen-Z consumers. The brand emphasizes ethically sourced natural ingredients, sustainable packaging, and a commitment to social responsibility through a partnership with Keep America Beautiful’s RETREET program. Fieldtrip offers an initial lineup of seven products, available online and expanding to retailers like Nordstrom and Macy's in August, with more products slated for release in Fall 2022.

feed.title: Teladoc hit with class-action suit alleging it misled investors
feed.summary: Teladoc is facing a new class-action lawsuit alleging that the company, along with its CEO and CFO, knowingly misled investors about its business prospects and downplayed competition. This suit follows a significant drop in Teladoc's stock price after the virtual care company missed revenue expectations and reported a $6.6 billion impairment charge related to its Livongo acquisition in its first-quarter results. The lawsuit claims investors bought shares at "artificially inflated prices" and suffered substantial losses, though Teladoc has called the litigation "frivolous."

feed.title: Amazon (AMZN) Gains as Stock Split Lowers Price Tag for Retail Buyers
feed.summary: Amazon's stock surged after a 20-for-1 split, making shares more accessible to retail investors. This marks the company's first split in over two decades, leading to increased trading volume and outperforming the Nasdaq 100 Index. The move is expected to attract greater retail interest, potentially acting as a sentiment catalyst.

feed.title: Peloton Appoints Liz Coddington as Chief Financial Officer
feed.summary: Peloton Interactive, Inc. announced the appointment of Liz Coddington as its new Chief Financial Officer, effective June 13, 2022. Ms. Coddington brings over two decades of financial experience from companies like Amazon Web Services, Walmart.com, and Netflix. She succeeds Jill Woodworth, who will transition to a consultant role to ensure a smooth handover and support the reporting of FY2022 financial results.

feed.title: Netflix Gearing Up for Formula 1 Rights Push
feed.summary: Netflix is reportedly vying for the U.S. broadcast rights to Formula 1, marking its first potential move into live sports. The streaming giant is competing with ESPN, Amazon, and NBCUniversal for the rights, which are sought at around $100 million annually by F1's parent company, Liberty Media. This interest comes as F1's popularity in the U.S. has surged, partly due to Netflix's "Drive to Survive" docuseries, and coincides with Netflix's plans to introduce an ad-supported tier.

feed.title: U.S. Supreme Court rules Southwest Airlines cannot force wage suit into arbitration
feed.summary: The U.S. Supreme Court ruled 8-0 that Southwest Airlines cannot force a baggage handler's class action lawsuit over overtime pay into private arbitration, exempting them from a federal law due to their involvement in interstate commerce. This decision has potential implications for other companies like Amazon and Uber, as it suggests that various transportation workers may also be exempt from mandatory arbitration for wage claims, leading to more class actions rather than individual arbitrations.

feed.title: XPO Logistics Appoints Yoav Amiel as Chief Information Officer
feed.summary: XPO Logistics has appointed Yoav Amiel as Chief Information Officer for its planned spin-off of the asset-light brokered transportation platform. Amiel, who previously led the technology organization for XPO’s North American transportation division, has been critical in developing the XPO Connect digital brokerage platform. This move supports the spin-off's creation of two separate, publicly traded companies focused on North American growth.

feed.title: With shares of Kansas City’s Cerner turned over, sale to Oracle will close Wednesday
feed.summary: Oracle's acquisition of Cerner Corporation for $28.3 billion is set to formally close on Wednesday, June 8th, following a successful stock tender offer. This acquisition marks Oracle's largest ever and signifies its entry into the healthcare market, with Cerner continuing as a dedicated subsidiary and Oracle pledging to grow jobs in Kansas City. The deal concludes Cerner's status as the largest private employer under local control in Kansas City, a company founded in 1979.

feed.title: Oracle closes $28B deal to buy EHR giant Cerner
feed.summary: Oracle has finalized its $28.3 billion acquisition of health IT company Cerner, marking its largest acquisition to date and a significant move to expand into the healthcare market. The deal, which involved Oracle finalizing a stock tender offer with 69.2% of Cerner shares, aims to leverage Cerner as an "anchor asset" to scale Oracle's cloud business in hospitals and health systems. This acquisition positions Oracle to transform healthcare delivery through new information systems and addresses the growing trend of big tech companies investing heavily in the healthcare IT sector.

feed.title: Teladoc Health faces class action lawsuit alleging it misled investors
feed.summary: Teladoc Health is facing a class action lawsuit alleging the company, its CEO Jason Gorevic, and CFO Mala Murthy misled investors. The suit claims they failed to disclose that increasing competition was negatively impacting its BetterHelp mental health and chronic care segments, leading to unsustainable growth projections. This alleged misrepresentation resulted in significant investor losses and a $6.6 billion non-cash goodwill impairment charge related to its 2020 Livongo acquisition.

feed.title: Kohl’s Corp. negotiating company sale to owner of The Vitamin Shoppe
feed.summary: Kohl’s Corp. has entered into exclusive negotiations with Franchise Group, Inc., owner of The Vitamin Shoppe, regarding a potential acquisition at $60 per share. This development comes amid ongoing shareholder pressure and previous attempts to acquire the company. While the deal’s certainty is unknown, an expert noted the buyer might see an undervalued asset rather than bringing strategic advantages to Kohl's.

feed.title: Amazon Sued Over 'Bait-And-Switch' Whole Foods Fee
feed.summary: Amazon is facing a putative class action lawsuit filed by an Amazon Prime member in Washington federal court. The lawsuit alleges that Amazon engaged in "bait-and-switch" false advertising by promising free grocery services for Whole Foods Market orders but then added a $9.95 service fee. The plaintiff claims this practice constitutes false advertising.

feed.title: Mississippi REIT gets chunk of SF industrial market
feed.summary: EastGroup Properties, a Mississippi-based REIT, acquired Tulloch Corp. in Oakland for approximately $415 million, gaining 14 industrial properties totaling 1.7 million square feet, predominantly in the San Francisco Bay Area. This acquisition significantly boosts EastGroup's California portfolio, increasing its holdings to 7.6 million square feet. Despite recent market shifts, EastGroup remains optimistic about the Bay Area industrial market due to strong tenant demand.

feed.title: Etsy sellers getting squeezed by ‘Amazon effect’
feed.summary: Etsy sellers are facing increasing pressure due to rising fees, consumer expectations for fast and free shipping, and competition from larger platforms like Amazon, leading to shrinking profit margins. The article highlights the experiences of sellers who participated in a strike, dealt with copyright infringement issues, and are considering moving to alternative platforms like Shopify to regain control over their businesses and artistic integrity. This "Amazon effect" is forcing many small business owners to adapt or seek new avenues to sell their handmade products.

feed.title: Amazon’s former No. 2 Dave Clark just joined a Bay Area logistics startup as co-CEO
feed.summary: Dave Clark, formerly Amazon's consumer chief, has joined Flexport Inc. as co-CEO. He will serve in this role for six months starting September 1st, after which he will become the sole CEO, with current CEO Ryan Petersen transitioning to executive chairman. Clark's departure from Amazon comes amidst slowing online sales growth and an excess of warehouse space, concluding a two-decade career where he championed innovation in Amazon's fulfillment and transportation sectors.

feed.title: Ex-Amazon worker accused of stealing personal data of 100M Capital One customers goes on trial
feed.summary: A former Amazon software engineer, Paige Thompson, is on trial for allegedly stealing personal data from over 100 million Capital One customers in one of the largest data breaches in US history. Prosecutors claim she intended to commit identity theft and profit, while her defense argues she was acting as a "white-hat hacker" trying to expose vulnerabilities in the bank's system. Thompson faces 10 counts of computer fraud, wire fraud, and identity theft, and if convicted, could face up to 30 years in prison.

feed.title: Stellantis Stock Is Undervalued, Even as It Catches Up in the Electric Vehicle Market
feed.summary: Stellantis, formed from the 2021 merger of Fiat Chrysler and Peugeot, is making an aggressive push into the electric vehicle market after being a laggard. Despite its efforts to catch up, Morningstar analysts consider Stellantis stock undervalued, trading at a significant discount to its peers. The company plans an all-electric lineup for its luxury brands by 2024 and aims for 50% EV sales in North America by 2030, alongside ambitious carbon reduction and revenue growth targets.

feed.title: Kroger is now delivering in South Florida
feed.summary: Kroger has launched online grocery delivery services in South Florida through a new 60,000-square-foot spoke facility in Miami, which supports its automated customer fulfillment center in Groveland, Florida. This expansion is part of Kroger's aggressive growth strategy in Florida, utilizing a hub-and-spoke network to deliver groceries to areas hundreds of miles from its CFCs. The company aims to compete with rivals like Amazon and Walmart by focusing on next-day delivery, a wide assortment, competitive pricing, and its partnership with Ocado, particularly in markets where it lacks physical stores.

feed.title: Dow dives 800 points, S&P 500 posts worst week since January after inflation hits 40-year high
feed.summary: U.S. stocks fell sharply on Friday, with the Dow dropping 880 points and the S&P 500 completing its worst week since January, following a higher-than-expected inflation report for May. The consumer price index reached its highest level since 1981, showing an 8.6% year-over-year increase, fueling concerns about a potential recession and prompting fears of a more aggressive Federal Reserve. Tech stocks, banks, and cyclical stocks were particularly impacted as the 2-year Treasury yield surged above 3%.

feed.title: Fortinet (FTNT) to Split Stock in 5 to Attract More Investors
feed.summary: Fortinet (FTNT) announced a five-for-one forward stock split, effective June 22, aiming to make its shares more accessible to employees and retail investors. This move is expected to boost demand and further increase share prices, building on its impressive 710% return over the past five years. Other tech giants like Alphabet, Amazon, and NVIDIA have also recently undertaken stock splits for similar reasons.

feed.title: Hack Into Quantum Computing Boom With QQQ
feed.summary: Quantum computing, a disruptive technology with significant growth potential, is still in its early stages but offers various use cases. While some speculative companies exist, major players in this field are large-cap companies. The Invesco QQQ Trust (QQQ) and Invesco NASDAQ 100 ETF (QQQM) provide investors with exposure to quantum computing through their holdings in established tech giants like Microsoft, Amazon, Alphabet, Nvidia, and Honeywell.

feed.title: Fortinet (FTNT) to Split Stock in 5 to Attract More Investors
feed.summary: Fortinet (FTNT) announced a five-for-one forward stock split to make its shares more accessible to employees and retail investors, with stockholder approval scheduled for June 17. If approved, the stock price will drop from approximately $300 to $60 per share. This move follows similar stock splits by other major tech companies like Alphabet, Amazon, and NVIDIA, aiming to boost demand and potentially increase share prices.

feed.title: Lululemon leases an additional 120K square feet of office space
feed.summary: Lululemon Athletica Inc. has signed one of Vancouver's largest office lease deals since 2018, securing an additional 120,000 square feet across nine floors at Burrard Place. This transaction signals a strong commitment to office space by large firms, challenging the pandemic-driven narrative of reduced office demand. The new space is located near Lululemon's current headquarters and is scheduled for occupancy in late 2022.

feed.title: Walmart struggles to solve consumer needs in China
feed.summary: Walmart has faced persistent challenges in the Chinese market since opening its first store in 1996, struggling to compete with local retailers known for their diverse product offerings and fast home deliveries. The company's large hypermarket format is not appealing to Chinese consumers who prefer online shopping and local products. Additionally, Walmart has found itself navigating complex political tensions, including controversies over product sourcing from Xinjiang and increased regulatory scrutiny, despite China being crucial for its manufacturing supply chain and for observing e-commerce trends.

feed.title: Oracle’s Database Dominance Eroded by Rise of Cloud-First Rivals
feed.summary: Oracle's long-standing dominance in the database market is being challenged by cloud-first rivals offering more flexible and cheaper options. Companies like Shutterfly are migrating their data to cloud providers such as Amazon.com Inc., moving away from Oracle's traditional database products due to ease of use. Despite this trend, Oracle is still projected to report 4% sales growth.

feed.title: Judge Dismisses Class Action Lawsuit Filed Against GoodRx
feed.summary: A federal judge has dismissed a class action lawsuit filed against GoodRx Holdings, Inc. The lawsuit alleged that GoodRx made misleading statements and filed a misleading registration statement and prospectus regarding its initial public offering, particularly concerning the competitive threat posed by Amazon. The judge ruled that the plaintiffs failed to sufficiently plead facts establishing falsity, concrete knowledge by GoodRx of Amazon's plans, or scienter.

feed.title: System Report: American Eagle Outfitters embraces fulfillment at the edge
feed.summary: American Eagle Outfitters (AEO) is innovating its fulfillment strategy, moving beyond traditional distribution centers to embrace "fulfillment at the edge" to meet soaring e-commerce demands and customer expectations for speed. By acquiring Quiet Logistics and AirTerra, AEO is strategically positioning inventory closer to major metropolitan areas using a network of smaller fulfillment centers that leverage autonomous mobile robots and advanced software. This new approach, developed under Shekar Natarajan, aims to enhance efficiency, reduce delivery times, and potentially create a shared supply chain model with other retailers.

feed.title: Amazon Prime Air prepares for drone deliveries
feed.summary: Amazon's Prime Air drone delivery service is preparing to launch in Lockeford, California, marking a significant step in making drone deliveries a reality after nearly a decade of development. The service aims to deliver packages quickly and safely, leveraging advanced sense-and-avoid technology to navigate obstacles and ensure safe landings without human observers. Lockeford residents will provide crucial feedback to help scale the service, which has earned an FAA air carrier certificate through rigorous testing and innovation.

feed.title: Semiconductor giant Marvell plans ‘significant expansion’ of Kanata footprint after acquisition
feed.summary: Marvell, a U.S. semiconductor company, is significantly expanding its presence in Canada, particularly in Kanata, following its acquisition of local microchip design firms. The company plans to build out its offices in Ottawa, Toronto, and Vancouver to develop semiconductor technology for cloud, 5G, and automotive markets. Marvell expects to leverage Ottawa's tech talent and academic partnerships for its growth, with a focus on cutting-edge technologies.

feed.title: Grassroots mojo and 4 other reasons Starbucks workers have been so successful unionizing
feed.summary: Starbucks Workers United has achieved significant success in unionizing stores across the U.S., winning over 100 elections since December 2021. This unexpected success is attributed to a shift in public sentiment towards unions, a replicable worker-driven organizing model, Starbucks' progressive brand attracting pro-union employees, a strong sense of community among baristas, and a decentralized, grassroots approach to organizing. This movement could signal a broader union revival in the service sector.

feed.title: Stipends for remote work emerge as polarizing issue
feed.summary: The rise of permanent remote work has sparked debate over whether companies should reimburse employees for home office expenses like internet and electricity, especially if remote work is by choice. This issue presents legal implications, with some states requiring reimbursement, and has led to lawsuits, such as one against Amazon in California. Experts suggest that while legal obligations vary, decisions around reimbursement will also influence employee morale and experience.

feed.title: Steve Rendle’s Pay at VF Tops $15 Million
feed.summary: VF Corp. CEO Steve Rendle received $15.4 million in total compensation last year, a 2.3% decrease from the previous year. The majority of his compensation, $10.3 million, was in stock and option awards, tying his pay to shareholder performance. Rendle is navigating challenges like inflation and supply chain issues for VF's diverse brand portfolio, which includes Supreme, Vans, and The North Face.

feed.title: Edgewell debuts Gen Z-focused skincare brand, Fieldtrip
feed.summary: Edgewell has launched Fieldtrip, a new clean skincare brand aimed at Gen Z consumers. The brand offers unisex products with luxury formulations under $25, initially sold direct-to-consumer and on Amazon, with plans to expand to Nordstrom and Macy's. Fieldtrip emphasizes sustainability and affordability, aligning with Gen Z's values.

feed.title: Drones will start delivering Amazon packages this year, company says
feed.summary: Amazon announced that it will begin delivering packages via its Prime Air drone service to residents in Lockeford, California, later this year. The company has spent nearly a decade developing its drone technology, which includes a sophisticated sense-and-avoid system to ensure safe operation. Amazon is working with the FAA and local officials to implement the service and plans to invest in the Lockeford community.

feed.title: Lululemon Goes Back to Work in Style with Massive New Vancouver Office
feed.summary: Lululemon Athletica Inc. is significantly expanding its real estate footprint in its hometown of Vancouver by leasing close to 120,000 sq. ft of office space in the new Burrard Place building. This deal is considered one of the largest office lease transactions in downtown Vancouver since the pandemic, signaling a commitment by large firms to office spaces despite ongoing debates about remote and hybrid work models. The expansion comes as Lululemon also makes headlines for other real estate ventures and new product releases.

feed.title: Newmark Completes Sale of Moffett Green, Fully-Leased Trophy Campus in Silicon Valley
feed.summary: Newmark has successfully completed the sale of Moffett Green, a 719,037 square-foot, fully-leased trophy office campus in Sunnyvale, California, to CommonWealth Partners, LLC. The transaction, which represents the largest single-asset investment office sale in Silicon Valley history, involved Meta Platforms, Inc. as the long-term tenant. Steven Golubchik and his team at Newmark facilitated the deal, highlighting continued investor demand for prime assets in high-barrier-to-entry markets and the strong performance of Moffett Park.

feed.title: Next-Generation Adobe Analytics Delivers Customer Insights From Streaming Media and the Metaverse
feed.summary: Adobe has launched new services for Adobe Analytics, creating a unified workspace for brands to gather data and insights from various media, including the metaverse and streaming content. This update allows for seamless data migration from other analytics platforms, ensuring compliance with regulations like GDPR and CCPA. By supporting emerging channels, Adobe Analytics aims to provide comprehensive omnichannel analysis through Customer Journey Analytics, helping businesses understand evolving consumer behaviors and deliver personalized experiences.

feed.title: eBay Inc. stock falls Tuesday, underperforms market
feed.summary: eBay Inc. (EBAY) stock dropped 0.82% to $42.58 on Tuesday, underperforming the broader market as the S&P 500 and Dow Jones Industrial Average also saw declines. This marked the fourth consecutive day of losses for eBay, with the stock closing significantly below its 52-week high. Competitors showed mixed performance, with Amazon.com Inc. falling, while Walmart Inc. and Costco Wholesale Corp. rose.

feed.title: The Surprising Case for Stronger E-commerce Growth
feed.summary: Despite a recent slump in e-commerce stocks and slowing economic activity, Morgan Stanley forecasts continued strong growth for e-commerce, projecting an increase from $3.3 trillion today to $5.4 trillion in 2026. This growth is driven by a permanent behavioral shift to online shopping, increasing penetration in both developed and emerging markets, and technological improvements in logistics and digital payments.

feed.title: Everything You Wanted to Know About Bear Markets
feed.summary: This article discusses the characteristics of bear markets, noting that while bull markets are similar, bear markets each have unique causes. Author Frank Holmes explains that the current bear market is due to pandemic-related liquidity, rampant inflation, and aggressive central bank actions, including a recent significant interest rate hike by the Federal Reserve. He advises investors to stay diversified, consider adding gold to their portfolios, and maintain a positive outlook given that bear markets are typically short-lived and can present buying opportunities.

feed.title: Meet Naima Greenwood | President & Chief Operating Officer, Yardstick Management
feed.summary: The article features an interview with Naima Greenwood, President & Chief Operating Officer of Yardstick Management, the nation's leading Black-owned management consulting firm. Greenwood discusses the firm's significant impact on diversity, equity, and inclusion within global organizations like Amazon and Netflix, and their commitment to leveling the playing field for marginalized communities. She also shares personal insights about Atlanta, where Yardstick Management is headquartered, and highlights the important community work of the Villages of Carver YMCA.

feed.title: Sonos tips: how to stereo pair, connect to a TV, and more
feed.summary: This article provides a comprehensive guide to getting the most out of a Sonos system, covering frequently asked questions and offering 25 tips and tricks. It details aspects like Bluetooth connectivity, using Sonos without Wi-Fi, connecting to a TV, app usage, waterproofing, stereo pairing, and enhancing sound quality with Trueplay and external DACs. The guide also touches on streaming services, voice control, and integrating vinyl with Sonos, demonstrating the system's versatility.

feed.title: How to cancel Amazon Prime: Here's how to end your membership in a few steps
feed.summary: This article provides a simple, three-step guide on how to cancel an Amazon Prime membership. It details logging into Amazon, navigating to the Prime account settings, and selecting the "End membership" option. The piece also notes that benefits will continue until the end of the current billing cycle.

feed.title: hololive production Announces New Apparel Sales on Merch by Amazon
feed.summary: hololive production has announced a new line of apparel featuring various talents, which will be available globally via Merch by Amazon starting June 16, 2022. The white T-shirts depict talents like Tokino Sora, Robocosan, and Hoshimachi Suisei, and are shippable to customers in France, Germany, Italy, Japan, Spain, the United Kingdom, and the United States. Merch by Amazon handles production, sales, and shipping of these creator-designed products, offering standard Amazon shipping options.
