feed.title: Instead of IPL, Amazon wants to spend money building e-com biz
feed.summary: Amazon has decided against bidding for media rights to the Indian Premier League, opting instead to invest billions into its e-commerce business in India. The company, led by Manish Tiwary, aims to expand its reach beyond major cities to non-English speaking, less affluent populations in rural areas, targeting an additional 100 million shoppers. This strategy involves initiatives like "Smart Commerce" to digitize small merchants and using local influencers.

feed.title: Amazon Prime announces 2022 Prime Day dates will be held on July 12, 13
feed.summary: Amazon announced that its 2022 Prime Day sales event will take place on July 12 and 13. The 48-hour event, starting at 3 AM ET, will offer discounts across various categories and include Poland and Sweden for the first time. The annual event aims to boost Prime subscriptions and generate significant sales, impacting rival retailers who often hold their own sales concurrently.

feed.title: Canada's Telus strikes C$2.9 bln deal for LifeWorks in healthcare push
feed.summary: Canadian wireless carrier Telus Corp is acquiring LifeWorks Inc for C$2.9 billion, aiming to leverage the increasing demand for mental health services from employers, a trend exacerbated by the COVID-19 pandemic. The deal will combine LifeWorks with Telus Health, expanding its virtual healthcare offerings and aiming for annual savings of C$170 million to C$200 million over the next three to five years, including a significant presence in the U.S.

feed.title: The Big Interview: Expedia Group CTO Rathi Murthy
feed.summary: Expedia Group CTO Rathi Murthy discusses the company's "Expedia Open World" vision, a new API-centric, modular travel platform designed to allow more flexible integration for partners. She details the challenges of this large-scale transformation while the company is actively operating, emphasizing a "people, process, technology" approach and an iterative, accountability-driven methodology. The article highlights Expedia's move to AWS and their focus on hiring diverse talent.

feed.title: Bluepeak rebrands from Vast Broadband, expanding internet in Sioux Falls
feed.summary: Vast Broadband, a Sioux Falls internet provider, has rebranded as Bluepeak to reflect its expansion efforts in Sioux Falls and other states. The company plans to build fiber-optic cables to improve service reliability and internet speed for both existing and future customers. Bluepeak currently serves about 8,000 people in Sioux Falls and anticipates construction to continue expanding northward through summer 2023.

feed.title: Dick’s Sporting Goods Expanding, Burlington Moving to Town Square
feed.summary: Dick's Sporting Goods is set to expand significantly in the Town Square Mall, taking over the neighboring Dollar Tree space. Additionally, Burlington is relocating its store from the Oakdale Mall in Johnson City to the Town Square Mall, occupying the former A.C. Moore Arts & Crafts location, with construction already underway.

feed.title: Ariana Grande Debuts Chapter 3 of R.E.M. Beauty with a Bang(s)
feed.summary: Ariana Grande's R.E.M. Beauty launched its third collection, 'Chapter 3: on your collar,' focusing on lip products. This collection, which includes five new formulas like lip oil, balm, liner, and lipsticks, follows the brand's 'drops' model and continues its extraterrestrial aesthetic. R.E.M. Beauty's initial collections, Chapters 1 and 2, are also available at Ulta stores.

feed.title: Former Amazon employee convicted in Capital One hack
feed.summary: A former Amazon Web Services employee, Paige Thompson, has been convicted of hacking into Capital One and stealing the data of over 100 million people, making it one of the largest data breaches in the U.S. Thompson was found guilty of seven federal crimes, including wire fraud, and her sentencing is set for September 15. Capital One has previously agreed to pay $190 million to settle a class-action lawsuit and an additional $80 million in regulatory fines related to the breach.

feed.title: Ex-Amazon employee convicted over 2019 Capital One breach
feed.summary: A former Amazon Web Services (AWS) employee, Paige Thompson, has been convicted of seven federal crimes related to the 2019 Capital One data breach that affected over 106 million accounts. The breach led to Capital One paying an $80 million penalty and a $190 million settlement for customer lawsuits. Thompson, who is scheduled for sentencing in September, exploited misconfigured AWS accounts to steal personal data and mine cryptocurrency.

feed.title: False Advertising Lawsuit Against Vital Farms Wins Right to Proceed
feed.summary: PETA Foundation lawyers and co-counsel achieved a legal victory as a motion to dismiss a class-action lawsuit against Vital Farms Inc. was denied. This decision allows the case to proceed, brought by consumers alleging they were misled by the company's false claims of ethical and humane treatment of hens. Vital Farms' eggs are widely sold at major grocery chains.

feed.title: Digital Pharmacy Market Growth, Drivers, and Opportunities
feed.summary: The global digital pharmacy market is projected to grow significantly from USD 96.5 billion in 2022 to USD 211.9 billion by 2027, driven by factors such as increasing consumer preference for online medicine purchases, especially post-COVID-19, market consolidations, and an aging population. North America currently holds the largest market share, while emerging markets like China and India present substantial opportunities. Key challenges include the presence of illegal pharmacies and the lack of comprehensive regulatory frameworks worldwide.

feed.title: Former AWS engineer convicted over hack that cost Capital One $270m
feed.summary: A former AWS engineer, Paige Thompson, has been convicted of seven counts of fraud for stealing personal data from over 100 million people, including Capital One customers, after identifying and exploiting misconfigured AWS accounts. The breach has cost Capital One more than $270 million in compensation and regulatory fines. Thompson, who also used the breached accounts for cryptojacking, is awaiting sentencing in September.

feed.title: Paige Thompson found guilty in 2019 Capital One data breach
feed.summary: Paige Thompson, a former Amazon engineer, has been convicted in the 2019 Capital One data breach that exposed data of over 100 million customers. The hack involved misconfigured AWS accounts and cost Capital One hundreds of millions in fines and settlements. Thompson was found guilty of wire fraud and multiple counts of unauthorized access to a protected computer and damaging a protected computer, though acquitted on other charges.

feed.title: Corsair Dark Core RGB Pro SE wireless gaming mouse review
feed.summary: The Corsair Dark Core RGB Pro SE is a heavy, feature-rich wireless gaming mouse offering excellent connectivity and ergonomics. While praised for its build quality, customizable RGB, and precise sensor, its significant weight (142g) and mediocre battery life (20 hours with RGB on) are notable drawbacks, especially for competitive FPS players. The review concludes that it's a great option for those who prefer comfortable, heavier mice for productivity and slower-paced games, rather than twitch shooters.

feed.title: First Watch Adds Bumble Executive Stephanie Lilak to Board of Directors
feed.summary: First Watch Restaurant Group has appointed Stephanie Lilak, Chief People Officer of Bumble Inc., to its Board of Directors, effective June 17, 2022. Lilak will join the Audit Committee and Compensation Committee, bringing extensive human resources experience from her roles at Bumble Inc., Dunkin’ Brands, and General Mills. Her appointment is expected to support First Watch’s growth and its people-centric "You First" culture.

feed.title: Oracle introduces lower-cost version of its full on-premises cloud stack
feed.summary: Oracle has introduced a more affordable version of its on-premises cloud stack, Dedicated Region Cloud@Customer, alongside a new rack-level offering called Oracle Compute Cloud@Customer. The new Dedicated Region Cloud@Customer reduces the required space and annual cost significantly, making Oracle's full public cloud services, including Fusion applications, accessible to a broader range of global companies for workloads that cannot fully migrate to the public cloud. Oracle Compute Cloud@Customer provides managed on-site computing and storage resources for smaller workloads, similar to offerings from AWS, Microsoft, and Google.

feed.title: Build a data pipeline on AWS with Kafka, Kafka connect and DynamoDB
feed.summary: This article provides a step-by-step guide to building a data pipeline on AWS using Kafka, Kafka Connect, and DynamoDB. It covers setting up MSK, MSK Connect, and integrating Datagen source connector with a DynamoDB sink connector. The guide also details infrastructure preparation using CloudFormation and testing the end-to-end pipeline.

feed.title: Virtual reality and indoor ‘tree houses’: Truist unveils banking tech center in uptown
feed.summary: Truist Bank has opened a new 100,000-square-foot Innovation and Technology Center in uptown Charlotte, aiming to fuse tech and finance for a better banking experience. The center features virtual reality labs, "tree houses," and collaborative spaces, intending to propel Truist into the future of digital banking despite recent low rankings in consumer satisfaction for its digital services. The bank also launched an "Innovators in Residence" program with partners like Verizon and Amazon Web Services to explore new technologies.

feed.title: Barack, Michelle Obama ditch Spotify for Amazon-owned Audible
feed.summary: Former President Barack Obama and former First Lady Michelle Obama are moving their podcast content from Spotify to Amazon-owned Audible. Their production company, Higher Ground, will create new audio content for Audible, a platform primarily known for audiobooks. The Obamas cited Audible's investment in lifting up voices and telling stories that entertain and inspire as reasons for the switch.

feed.title: MinIO extends Snowflake analysis to any data location
feed.summary: MinIO has partnered with Snowflake to enable Snowflake analytics on data stored in any location, not just within Snowflake's own environment. This partnership allows customers to leverage external table support in MinIO for cost-effective analysis of large datasets without moving them to the cloud. This provides flexibility similar to recent Snowflake partnerships with Dell and Pure Storage, offering various options for on-premises or cloud-based data analysis.

feed.title: Dickies is turning 100 years old. It’s gone viral with Gen Z
feed.summary: Dickies, the utilitarian workwear brand, is celebrating its 100th anniversary and has unexpectedly gone viral with Gen Z, particularly with its 874 trousers. This surge in popularity is attributed to a combination of celebrity dressing, collaborations, product seeding to Depop sellers, and organic TikTok trends, where young people are styling the affordably priced trousers in creative ways. The brand has capitalized on this by resharing user-generated content, launching new styles, and enabling affiliate marketing through platforms like Amazon, demonstrating how authentic connection with subcultures and accessibility can drive significant engagement among a new generation.

feed.title: Zscaler and AWS Expand Relationship
feed.summary: Zscaler and Amazon Web Services (AWS) have extended their partnership to provide unified cloud security solutions built on Zscaler’s Zero Trust architecture. These innovations aim to simplify cloud security operations, accelerate cloud adoption, and protect cloud workloads and 5G connections. The collaboration delivers a new Posture Control™ solution built on AWS, extends Zero Trust security to AWS workloads, and enables Zero Trust for private 5G using AWS Wavelength.

feed.title: Best Buy has Motorola's MA1 adapter back in stock, so grab it while you can
feed.summary: The Motorola MA1 wireless Android Auto adapter is currently back in stock at Best Buy, after frequently selling out quickly due to high demand. The adapter, which allows for wireless Android Auto connectivity, has garnered positive user reviews and is a popular item, making its availability at Best Buy a notable event for those seeking the sought-after device.

feed.title: Avnet, and Amazon Web Services enters into a global strategic partnership
feed.summary: Avnet and Amazon Web Services (AWS) have formed a global strategic partnership aimed at helping Original Equipment Manufacturers (OEMs) of IoT solutions accelerate their time to market. This collaboration will enable Avnet’s IoTConnect Platform to leverage AWS's extensive portfolio of services, creating a scalable and secure platform for application-specific usage. The partnership provides OEMs with pre-integrated and abstracted capabilities, such as device provisioning, multi-layer security, and business intelligence, allowing them to focus on differentiating their connected products.

feed.summary: ODP Corp., the owner of Office Depot and OfficeMax, has decided to remain a

feed.title: Despite Shopify’s Stock Split, Investors Should Look Elsewhere
feed.summary: Morningstar analyst Sandy Ward advises investors to look beyond Shopify's stock split, suggesting Amazon shares as a better alternative. Shopify's stock has plummeted significantly, and concerns about its financial outlook and a new share class cementing founder control make it a less attractive investment compared to Amazon, which offers greater financial certainty and diversified revenue streams. Despite a potential upside, Shopify is not among Morningstar's top stock picks due to slowing revenue growth and quarterly losses.

feed.title: Amazon has a plan to make Alexa mimic anyone's voice
feed.summary: Amazon is developing a new Alexa feature that will allow the voice assistant to mimic any voice after hearing less than a minute of audio. The company's senior vice president, Rohit Prasad, stated the goal is to "make the memories last" for those who have lost loved ones, particularly after the pandemic. This technology, however, raises concerns about its potential for abuse, such as creating deepfakes, an issue Microsoft has also addressed with its voice-parroting software.

feed.title: Here’s how much the Jif peanut butter recall could cost parent company JM Smucker
feed.summary: The J.M. Smucker Company could face a $125 million impact from the massive recall of nearly 50 Jif peanut butter products due to a salmonella outbreak. The recall, originating from the company's Lexington plant, led to a 15% drop in stock price. Production has resumed, and products are expected back on shelves shortly, with heightened food safety measures in place.

feed.title: Chinese DPU chip firm gains funds, unicorn status ...
feed.summary: Jaguar Microsystems, a Chinese Data Processing Unit (DPU) chip company founded in 2020 by former Broadcom executive Sunny Siu, has secured hundreds of millions of yuan in funding, propelling its valuation to unicorn status at approximately US$1.34 billion. The financing round was led by Tencent Holdings Ltd. and included other major investors. Jaguar Microsystems, which employs nearly 400 staff, released an FPGA version of its DPU in 2021 and plans for mass production of its system-chip version by 2023, primarily targeting cloud computing and internet companies, with Tencent expected to be a key customer.

feed.title: Por qué un empresario propone colocar "estatuas de Cristina Kirchner en cada rincón de Uruguay"
feed.summary: A Brazilian venture capitalist, Paulo Passoni, has provocatively suggested erecting statues of Cristina Kirchner across Uruguay. He argues that her policies have inadvertently driven a significant number of Argentine entrepreneurs and tech companies to relocate to Uruguay, appreciating its stable economic environment and clear rules. This migration has fostered a thriving tech ecosystem in Uruguay, benefiting the country by attracting talent and investment.

feed.title: JPMorgan Chase Joins Companies Paying Employees Who Travel for Abortions
feed.summary: JPMorgan Chase announced it would cover travel expenses for employees needing to travel out of state for abortions, expanding a benefit that covers services unavailable near an employee's home. This decision follows the Supreme Court's overturning of Roe v. Wade and aligns JPMorgan with other companies like Citigroup, Starbucks, Amazon, Tesla, and Yelp making similar pledges. The move addresses the implications of state-level abortion bans, with many states poised to restrict or ban abortions following the ruling.

feed.title: Seattle Pride’s Biggest Sponsors Also Give Big to Homophobic Politicians
feed.summary: This article exposes how major corporate sponsors of Seattle Pride, specifically Alaska Air Group, Chateau Ste. Michelle, and T-Mobile, also donate significant amounts of money to politicians who oppose LGBTQ+ rights. It details specific examples of these donations and the voting records of the politicians supported. The article questions the alignment of these corporations' actions with Pride values and notes that Seattle Pride is reviewing its corporate partnerships.

feed.title: Omnicom banks on Walmart, Instacart in latest commerce expansion
feed.summary: Omnicom Media Group (OMG) has expanded its commerce offerings by partnering with Walmart Connect and Instacart. The Walmart partnership focuses on cross-screen planning and connecting first-party advertiser data to Walmart's DSP, while the Instacart collaboration includes account management, product insights, and utilizing Omni's clean room infrastructure. These moves aim to deepen Omnicom's connected commerce capabilities and help advertisers navigate a privacy-centric marketing landscape.

feed.title: 3 Reasons to Buy TJX Companies, and 1 to Sell
feed.summary: TJX Companies, the parent company of TJ Maxx and Marshalls, is highlighted as a resilient brick-and-mortar retailer with an evergreen business model benefitting from the "retail apocalypse" and offering deeply discounted goods. The article outlines three reasons to buy the stock: its solid business model, robust post-lockdown recovery, and attractive valuation coupled with a decent dividend. The primary reason to sell is potential macroeconomic headwinds such as inflation, higher freight costs, and supply chain disruptions, which could impact its margins and inventory management.

feed.title: Private Prisons Are a Socially Responsible Investment, According to Bizarre Wall Street Measures
feed.summary: This article critiques the Environmental, Social, and Governance (ESG) investing framework, particularly highlighting how private prison company CoreCivic leveraged a "racial equity audit" to improve its public image and attract investment despite its controversial practices. It argues that ESG funds often engage in "greenwashing" and "socialwashing," allowing companies with questionable core business models to appear socially responsible through superficial metrics like diversity quotas, while critics assert that these measures enrich consultants and fund managers without achieving real social impact. The article further exposes the inconsistencies and lack of regulation in ESG rankings, showing how companies like Exxon Mobil and McDonald's can receive favorable ESG scores despite contributing to environmental or social problems, and how many ESG funds have higher fees than traditional index funds with similar holdings.

feed.title: CVS, Rite Aid ration contraceptive pills as demand surges
feed.summary: CVS Health Corp. and Rite Aid Corp. are limiting purchases of emergency contraceptive pills like Plan B to three per customer due to a surge in demand following the US Supreme Court decision overturning Roe v. Wade. Other chains, such as Walgreens, have not implemented purchase limits at this time, though some Walmart products have online purchase limits that may change with demand fluctuations. The increased demand for emergency contraception reflects preparations people are making in response to the ruling, which is expected to make abortions largely illegal in many states.

feed.title: Federal Realty Pandemic Program Produced Permanent Deals for 50% of Tenants
feed.summary: Don Wood, CEO of Federal Realty Investment Trust, discussed the company's temporary leasing program during the pandemic, which resulted in over half of the tenants transitioning to permanent deals. He also highlighted the acquisition of Kingstowne Towne Center in Virginia and the importance of ESG principles, noting the company's 13 megawatts of solar capacity.

feed.title: Kroger's automated grocery delivery warehouse opens in Pleasant Prairie
feed.summary: Kroger has opened a new automated grocery delivery warehouse in Pleasant Prairie, Wisconsin, in partnership with Ocado Group PLC. This facility is the fifth of its kind for Kroger and is expected to create approximately 250 jobs, serving customers in Wisconsin, northern Illinois, and northwest Indiana. The warehouse utilizes a robotic system called "The Hive" to efficiently sort and pack groceries for delivery.

feed.title: Most Powerful Women 2022
feed.summary: Cablefax celebrates its 2022 Most Powerful Women in Broadband in Media, recognizing top-performing female executives across various sectors. The magazine highlights "Glass Breakers" who have overcome barriers, along with Women’s Advancement Champions, a Mentor of the Year, and the "Rising Tide" Class, featuring up-and-coming women making significant contributions. The publication includes insights from honorees on their evolving definitions of success and experiences as the sole women in a room.

feed.title: Unicard and Amdocs announce account-based ticketing platform
feed.summary: Unicard and Amdocs have partnered to launch an account-based ticketing platform for multi-mode and multi-operator transportation services. The platform, introduced at the Transport Ticketing Global exhibition in London, integrates Unicard's ABT system with Amdocs' cloud-based payment platform to offer a seamless 'tap-in, tap-out' experience across various public transport options. Initially targeting city regions and local authorities in the UK, this collaboration aims to promote sustainable and flexible travel.

feed.title: DISA looks to install 10GB ethernet line from Equinix data center to DHS facility
feed.summary: The Defense Information Systems Agency (DISA) is seeking bids to install and maintain a 10GB ethernet line connecting an Equinix data center in Dallas, Texas, to a Department of Homeland Security (DHS) facility in Pensacola, Florida. This initiative supports DHS's ongoing cloud migration efforts, which involve shifting workloads from their current data centers to cloud providers like AWS. The move comes amid continued spending on existing facilities and some controversy surrounding cloud contracts with human rights groups and Google employees protesting deals with ICE.

feed.title: AWS: Amazon (AMZN) Cloud Unit on Course for $3 Trillion Value, Redburn Says
feed.summary: Amazon Web Services (AWS) is projected by Redburn Ltd. to reach a $3 trillion valuation, a figure nearly triple Amazon.com Inc.'s current total market capitalization. Analyst Alex Haissl suggests AWS is so dominant that Amazon might eventually consider spinning it off from its slower-growing e-commerce business. The report initiates coverage on the cloud-computing industry but does not specify a timeline for AWS to achieve this valuation.

feed.title: Self-driving truck firm Waymo to deliver goods for Wayfair on Interstate 45
feed.summary: Waymo, Alphabet Inc.'s self-driving technology unit, is partnering with J.B. Hunt Transport Services to deliver Wayfair goods on Interstate 45 between Houston and Dallas. This six-week pilot program, starting in July, will involve autonomous Class 8 trucks with specialists monitoring operations in the cab. The partnership builds on previous successful tests and aims to integrate autonomous freight movement into supply chains to meet capacity needs.

feed.title: BP, Shell to cover employee travel for treatment after Roe v. Wade
feed.summary: BP PLC has joined Shell PLC in committing to cover employee travel expenses for healthcare treatment following the Supreme Court's overturning of Roe v. Wade. Both European oil producers updated their healthcare plans to extend benefits for women needing to travel for services, though neither explicitly named abortion. This move comes as other major companies like Amazon, JPMorgan Chase, Tesla, and Walt Disney also updated their policies to cover travel costs for out-of-state abortion services, while U.S. oil majors have largely remained silent.

feed.title: The 13 Best Grill Brands
feed.summary: This article identifies and reviews 13 top grill brands, highlighting what makes each manufacturer stand out in the market. It discusses various types of grills, including charcoal, gas, pellet, and griddles, outlining their price ranges, top products, and unique features. The selection criteria prioritize durability, performance, versatility, and availability across different retailers, catering to diverse user needs and budgets.

feed.title: Corsair TC200 gaming chair review: "A great chair for both work and play"
feed.summary: The Corsair TC200 gaming chair offers significant improvements over its predecessor, the T3 Rush, particularly for larger users with its wider seat and back, and internal lumbar support. Reviewer Frederick Hillinger praises its all-day comfort for both work and gaming, despite the lumbar support not being adjustable. The chair is highly recommended for its strong value, high-quality materials, and thoughtful design that incorporates user feedback.

feed.title: Exploring Life & Business with Lily Sanchez of Lily Catherine
feed.summary: Lily Sanchez, at just 13, launched her business, Lily Catherine, specializing in handmade jewelry before expanding into accessories, clothing, and decor. She discusses her journey from selling beaded bracelets to classmates to establishing an online presence, joining farmers' markets, and stocking products in local boutiques. Sanchez emphasizes overcoming challenges like balance and social media marketing while highlighting the crucial support from her community and family.

feed.title: Frito-Lay CHRO: 'Everyone needs mental health support' | Human Resources Director
feed.summary: Frito-Lay, a division of PepsiCo, Inc., is actively addressing the trucking industry's challenges, including high attrition and mental health concerns, by investing in its drivers' well-being. CHRO Patrick McLaughlin highlights the company's comprehensive approach, which includes competitive benefits, work-life balance initiatives, and robust mental health support programs like meQ and Spring Health. This strategy aims to improve retention and ensure Frito-Lay remains an employer of choice in a volatile labor market.

feed.title: Is Augmented Reality the future of retail?
feed.summary: Augmented Reality (AR) is poised to revolutionize the retail industry by improving customer experience and conversion rates. Using just a smartphone, AR allows customers to virtually try on products like jewelry, clothing, furniture, and even cars within their own physical environment. This technology helps consumers make more informed purchasing decisions and offers businesses a significant increase in sales conversion, even for physical showrooms utilizing "Magic Mirror" devices.

feed.title: Cloudera embraces Apache Iceberg as cloud data lake evolves
feed.summary: Cloudera has announced support for Apache Iceberg, an open-source cloud data lake table format, within its Cloudera Data Platform. This move signifies Cloudera's continued evolution from its Hadoop roots towards modern cloud data lake technology. The company believes Iceberg enhances its ability to work with various cloud providers and analytical engines, addressing the growing need for flexible and structured data lake solutions in enterprise environments.

feed.title: How Nuuly is using technology to aid in sustainability tracking
feed.summary: Nuuly, a clothing rental service by Urban Outfitters, is leveraging cloud-based technology, specifically Google Cloud, to track clothing items and enhance sustainability efforts. By understanding customer behavior and garment lifecycles through data analytics, Nuuly aims to reduce waste and improve efficiency. This initiative aligns with a broader retail trend where companies are prioritizing ESG efforts, though many struggle with implementation and measurement of sustainability.

feed.title: Electronics companies dealing with a 'mountain of inventory'
feed.summary: Samsung Electronics and LG Electronics are currently experiencing record-high inventory levels due to a significant decrease in demand for electronic devices globally. This oversupply, impacting everything from smartphones to home appliances, is leading companies to cut orders from suppliers, reduce working hours, and is expected to negatively affect earnings and balance sheets. The article highlights how factors like inflation, China's lockdown, and geopolitical tensions have weakened consumer sentiment, resulting in a "mountain of inventory" that needs to be consumed before market balance can be restored.

feed.title: Amazon, Disney, AT&T Gave to Abortion Foes Like DeSantis While Vowing to Help Employees
feed.summary: Amazon, Disney, and AT&T, despite pledging to cover travel costs for employees seeking reproductive medical care, have also contributed financially to anti-abortion governors and political figures like Ron DeSantis. State campaign-finance records show these corporate giants supported leaders actively working to reduce access to abortions, creating a contradiction between their public stances and political donations.
